## Can you really make a coaching app without coding?

Yes. Most Indian educators who have their own app today did not write a line of code; they used a platform that already had the app built and filled it with their own content and brand. What you choose is not whether to code, but who builds and maintains the app for you.

A coaching app looks simple from the outside: a login screen, a list of courses, videos, PDFs and a test. Underneath, it needs a server, video playback that works on slow mobile data, a payment flow that confirms UPI payments and opens access, a way to add new lessons without releasing a new app version, and regular updates so it keeps working on new Android and iOS versions. Writing all of that yourself is a software project, not a teaching task.

That is why no-code routes exist. In each of them the hard parts are built once and shared, and you work through forms and buttons: upload a video, set a price, choose a colour. The differences between routes come down to three questions: who builds the app, who can change it next month, and what else you still have to stitch together around it.

Educators we work with often start with the wrong question, "which app should I build?", when the useful one is "where will my students learn, pay and come back every week?" The app is the front door. The course library, tests, live classes and checkout behind it are what make it worth opening.






## Three ways to build a coaching app: agency, no-code builder or academy platform

You can hire an agency or freelancer to build a custom app, assemble one yourself in a general no-code app builder, or use an academy platform where a white-label coaching app comes with your LMS. Each fits a different educator.



Same goal, different work for you. Example comparison; times are illustrative.



### 1. Hire an agency or freelancer (custom build)

A developer team designs and codes an app to your specification. You get exactly what you asked for, and you pay for every part of it: design, build, testing, store publishing, hosting, and then every change and update after launch. Quotes vary so widely with scope that a single number is misleading; our guide to white label coaching app development cost in India lists the line items to ask about and what vendors publish. The catch most educators meet later is not the first invoice but the second: a new feature, a broken payment flow or an Android update means another ticket and another wait.



### 2. Use a no-code app builder

General app builders let you drag screens together without code. They are built for every kind of business, so a coaching app is something you assemble: you design the screens, then find a way to add a course library, video playback, tests, a checkout that opens access after payment, and a website. That can work for a simple content app, but educators usually discover that the hard parts of a coaching app are exactly the ones a generic builder leaves to them.



### 3. Use an academy platform with a white-label app

An academy platform (an LMS made for educators) gives you courses, tests, live classes, payments and a website as one system, and the student app is part of it. A white label coaching app means the app carries your academy's name, logo and colours, not the platform's. You change content and settings yourself in the platform's studio, and new lessons appear in the app without a new release. The trade-off: you work within what the platform offers rather than designing every screen from scratch.

## What does a coaching app for teachers need?

A coaching app for teachers needs eight basics: student login, a course library, video lessons, PDF notes, tests, live classes, UPI and card payments, and your own brand. Everything else is a later decision.



The eight basics students expect on day one. Studio preview · sample data.


- Student login: each student has an account that remembers what they bought and where they stopped.

- Course library: courses split into modules in syllabus order, so a student always knows what comes next.

- Video lessons: recorded lessons that play smoothly on a basic Android phone on mobile data.

- PDF notes: chapter notes, formula sheets and previous-year questions readable on a 6-inch screen.

- Tests: chapter quizzes and timed mock tests with answers, the part exam students return to most.

- Live classes: a weekly doubt class or revision session, so the course feels taught, not just sold.

- Payments: UPI and card checkout that opens the course automatically once the payment succeeds.

- Your brand: your academy name, logo and colours, so students know whose app they installed.


On AllCoaching all eight sit in one studio. Videos come in through YouTube and are unlimited on every plan, PDF notes and test series live in the Content section, live classes run through YouTube Live, Zoom or the built-in live room with no hour caps, and UPI or card checkout opens access on its own, with payouts through Razorpay. The same courses appear on your academy website and in your app. For the course itself, our guide to creating your first online course covers structure, recording and tests in detail.

## How do you brand a white label coaching app?

Brand a white label coaching app with four decisions made before you open the studio: an academy name students can say and type, a square logo that reads at icon size, one main colour plus one accent, and a domain that matches the name.



Decide the brand kit once, use it everywhere. Studio preview · sample data.



### The academy name

Use the name students already know you by. If your YouTube channel is "Sharma Sir Maths", the app should not be called something new and clever; students search for the name they know. Keep it short enough to fit under an app icon on a phone home screen, and check the matching domain is available before you settle on it.



### The logo

An app icon is small. A logo with a long name written across it turns into a smudge at icon size. Make a square version: an initial, a simple mark or a short word on a solid colour. Test it by shrinking it to the size of a fingernail on your own phone screen.



### Colours

Pick one main colour for buttons and headings and one accent. Check that white text is readable on your main colour; very light yellows and pastels often fail on a bright phone screen outdoors.



### Consistency

Use the same name, logo and colours on your app, website, YouTube channel art, Instagram profile and WhatsApp display picture. When a student taps a link and sees the same face and name they followed on YouTube, they trust the install.






## Do you need an Android app, an iOS app or both?

Start with Android: for most Indian coaching students, especially in tier-2 and tier-3 cities, an Android phone is the device they study on. Add iOS when a meaningful share of your students, often working adults, CAT or CLAT aspirants and students abroad, ask for it.



Prices exclude GST. Growth and Pro can also be paid yearly with 2 months free.



### What the stores require if you publish yourself

If you build an app yourself or through an agency, you deal with the stores directly. Google Play's help centre states:


"There is a US$25 one-time registration fee."

Google Play Console Help1

Google also asks personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 to run a closed test with at least 12 testers for at least 14 days before the app can go live.2 Apple's Developer Program costs 99 USD a year.3 And apps need regular updates: Google Play requires new apps and app updates to target a recent Android API level,5 so an app nobody maintains eventually cannot ship updates.

Apple's guidelines matter for template-based apps in particular. Guideline 4.2.6 reads: "Apps created from a commercialized template or app generation service will be rejected unless they are submitted directly by the provider of the app's content."4 Whichever provider you choose, ask whose developer account the app is published under and what happens to it if you leave.

## How do you get students to install your coaching app?

Give students a reason before you ask for the install: send them from YouTube, WhatsApp and Instagram to a free demo lesson on your academy website, and ask them to install the app once they have something to come back to. "Download my app" alone rarely works; "the notes and test for today's class are in the app" does.



One link, everywhere your students already are. Example path, illustrative. Logos belong to their owners.



### From YouTube

Put your academy link in the first two lines of every video description and in a pinned comment. At the end of a useful free video, say exactly what the student gets in the app: "the PDF of these 20 questions and a timed test are free inside the app". A specific reason converts better than a general request.



### From WhatsApp

Your existing batch group is the fastest first 50 installs. Move one thing into the app and announce it: this week's notes, the mock test, or the live class link. Keep the group for announcements and point every announcement to the app. Many students resist leaving WhatsApp at first; move them with content, not with rules.



### From Instagram

Use the bio link for your academy website, and stories with a link sticker on days you post a new test or live class. Reels bring new people; the bio link turns the interested ones into students.



### In class

If you teach offline, give the first five minutes of one class to installing together: students open the link, log in, and open the free lesson while you are in the room. Educators we work with often find this single step does more than a week of posts.

## Common mistakes when making a coaching app

The most common coaching app mistakes are launching the app before there is content, chasing features instead of the basics, ignoring the website, choosing a name students do not recognise, going quiet after launch, and not checking how to take your data with you.



Six mistakes we see most often, and the fix for each.


- App before content. An empty app gets uninstalled. Upload one complete course with notes and tests before you share the link.

- Ten features, no plan. Start with the eight basics above. Add more only when students ask for something twice.

- No website. Links from YouTube and Instagram open in a browser. Without a website and a demo lesson, the student has nothing to see before installing.

- An unclear app name. Use the name students already follow, not a new brand they have never heard of.

- Launch and forget. A weekly live class and a new test every week give students a reason to open the app. Without them, installs turn into uninstalls.

- No way to leave. Before you sign with anyone, ask how you export your students and content. On AllCoaching your content and student data stay exportable.



"Students do not open an app because it exists. They open it because today's notes, today's test and today's class are inside."

Amit Ratan, Founder & CEO, AllCoaching






## When is a custom-built coaching app worth it?

A custom app is worth it when you need software no platform offers, such as a unique learning tool, deep integration with your institute's own systems, or a design you must control screen by screen, and you have the budget and a team to maintain it.

Large multi-centre institutes sometimes reach that point. For an individual educator or a small institute starting out, it usually makes sense to launch on a platform first, learn what your students actually use, and only then decide whether anything is missing. If you later outgrow it, having your content and student data exportable keeps that option open.

If you are still deciding what kind of business you are building, our explainer on what an online academy is shows how the website, app, courses and payments fit together.






## Glossary


White-label app
An app built and maintained by a platform but published under your academy's name, logo and colours.
No-code
Building software through forms, settings and drag and drop instead of writing programming code.
LMS (learning management system)
Software that holds courses, lessons, tests and student progress, and controls who can access what.
App builder
A general tool for assembling an app from ready-made screens and blocks, not specific to teaching.
Developer account
The account on Google Play or the Apple Developer Program that an app is published under.
Platform fee
The percentage a platform keeps from each sale, on top of a yearly plan where one applies.
Demo lesson
A free lesson that lets students judge your teaching before they buy or install.
Custom domain
Your own web address, such as youracademy.in, connected to your academy website.

# WhatsApp Group to Online Academy: Step-by-Step Guide (2026)

**Source:** https://allcoaching.in/blog/whatsapp-group-to-online-academy  
**Published:** 2026-10-27T09:00:00+05:30  
**Updated:** 2026-10-27T09:00:00+05:30  
**Author:** Amit Ratan, Founder &amp; CEO, AllCoaching  

**Summary:** Move a paid coaching batch from WhatsApp groups to your own online academy: audit your tools, upload old notes as a course, add UPI checkout, set a switch-over date.

Amit RatanUpdated 27 Oct 2026 · 21 min read


On this page


Start your online academy today. 7 days free.

Start free trial


To move a paid coaching batch from a WhatsApp group to your own online academy, list every tool the batch uses today, set up the academy, upload your old lessons and notes as one organised course, add UPI and card checkout, announce a switch-over date to your students with a clear message, keep the WhatsApp group only for announcements, and personally follow up with anyone who has not moved. Done in that order, most batches move in two to four weeks without losing students.

Perhaps this is your week. Admissions come through a Google Form. Fees arrive on UPI and the proof arrives as a screenshot in your personal chat. The Zoom link goes into the group every evening. Notes sit in a Drive folder that three people have edit access to. A new student joins in the third month and asks for everything from the first two. None of this is wrong; it is how a huge number of Indian educators started teaching online, because WhatsApp is where students already are.

The trouble starts when the batch grows. This guide names the problems honestly, then gives you an eight-step migration plan, ready-to-send message templates for your students, a four-week timeline and the mistakes to avoid. It is written for exam educators (SSC, NEET, JEE, banking, state PSC) and skill educators (spoken English, yoga, music, coding) alike, and it works the same way if your batch lives on Telegram.






## Key takeaways


- WhatsApp is good at conversation, not at running a paid course: it has no checkout, no course library in order, no tests and no record of who has paid.

- The biggest hidden cost is fee checking by hand: matching UPI screenshots to bank entries, then adding each student and resending old links, every batch.

- Links leak: Google Drive's "anyone with the link" setting and YouTube unlisted videos can both be opened by anyone the link is forwarded to.

- Do not delete the group. Keep WhatsApp for reminders and alerts, and move fees, lessons, notes, tests and live class links into your academy.

- Pick one switch-over date, announce it about two weeks ahead, honour what current students already paid, and follow up one by one.

- Students do not have to install anything: your academy website opens in the phone's browser, and your own Android app is there for those who want it.

- On AllCoaching you sign up, choose a plan, upload your course, connect your domain and start selling, after a 7-day free trial with no card.







## How do you move from a WhatsApp group to your own online academy?

Audit what you use, set up the academy, upload old content as a course, set a price with UPI checkout, invite current students, keep WhatsApp for announcements, switch over on a fixed date, then follow up. Each step below has its own section.


- Audit what you useList every tool, piece of content, student and fee the batch runs on today in one sheet.

- Set up your academySign up, choose a plan, add your name and logo, and connect your own domain.

- Upload old content as a courseRebuild Drive and YouTube material into modules with lessons in order, PDF notes, tests and a free demo lesson.

- Set a price and UPI checkoutKeep your current fee, add UPI and card checkout, and test one real payment with a friend.

- Invite existing studentsSend a clear announcement with one date and one link, and honour what current students already paid.

- Keep WhatsApp for announcementsMake the group admin-only or use a Channel for reminders, alerts and links back to the academy.

- Switch over on a fixed dateAfter the date, new fees, notes and live class links are only in the academy.

- Follow up one by oneMessage or call every student who has not signed in, and review the move after a month.


The order matters. Educators who announce first and build later end up sending half-finished links to a whole batch. Educators who build quietly for a week, test a payment with a friend and only then announce usually move most of their students in the first few days.

When educators move a batch to AllCoaching, the part they worry about most is students. The part that actually takes time is the content: turning two years of Drive folders and forwarded PDFs into modules a new student can follow. Plan your week around that.






## What are the problems with running paid coaching on WhatsApp groups?

The main WhatsApp coaching problems are manual fee checks, links that can be forwarded to anyone, new students who cannot see old notes, group size limits that split a batch, phone numbers visible to every member and no way to track progress. Each one is small with 20 students and painful with 200.



The stitched-together setup on the left, one academy on the right. Illustrative. Logos belong to their owners.



### 1. Fees are checked by hand

A student pays on UPI, sends a screenshot, and you open your bank app to match the amount and the name. Then you note it in a sheet and add the student to the group. A screenshot is a picture, not a payment record; it can be old, cropped or for a different amount, and you only find out when you check. At the end of the month, "who has not paid" becomes a scroll through chats.



### 2. Links travel further than you want

Paid material on WhatsApp usually means a Drive link or a YouTube link. Google's own help page describes the "Anyone with the link" setting plainly: "Anyone on the internet who has the link can open the file without signing in to a Google Account."1 YouTube says unlisted videos "can be seen and shared by anyone with the link".2 Once a link is in a group, any member can forward it to a friend who never paid.



### 3. New students cannot see the old notes

A WhatsApp group is a timeline, not a library. A student who joins in month three finds PDFs, links and voice notes buried hundreds of messages up, if they can see them at all, and asks you to resend everything. You end up re-posting the same material for every late joiner.



### 4. Groups have a size limit

WhatsApp groups have a member cap, and big batches end up split into "Batch A" and "Batch B" groups that you post into twice. Telegram channels avoid the cap but bring the same link-sharing and fee problems.



### 5. Members can see each other's phone numbers

In a regular group, members can generally see each other's numbers. For a batch of teenagers or working adults who do not know each other, that is personal information shared more widely than anyone intended, and it is also how your students get spam from strangers who joined the group.



### 6. You cannot see progress

You cannot tell who watched yesterday's recording, who opened the PDF or who skipped the last three tests. Without that, you only find a weak student when the exam result arrives.



Problem on WhatsAppWhat it costs youWhat fixes it in an academy

The six problems in one table.







## When should you move students from WhatsApp to an app or academy?

Move when you spend more time managing the batch than teaching it: when fee checks take more than an evening a month, when you post the same thing in two groups, or when you want to sell a recorded course to students you will never meet. If you teach one small batch of friends' children, WhatsApp may be all you need for now.

Signs it is time:


- You have more than one group for the same course.

- You have found your paid PDFs in a group you did not create.

- Students ask "sir, can you send the old notes again" every week.

- You want to sell last year's recordings as a course, not just run a live batch.

- You want students from other cities to find and pay you without a phone call.


The usual worry is that students will not want another app. They do not need one. Your academy is a website first, and it opens in the phone's browser from a link you send on WhatsApp. If that worry is the main thing stopping you, read our guide on what to do when students won't download your coaching app and just want WhatsApp; it covers that question in detail. This guide is about the move itself.






## Step 1: Audit what your batch runs on today

Before you build anything, write down every tool the batch uses, every piece of content you have, every student and what each student has paid for. This list becomes your migration checklist.



Give each tool a new home. WhatsApp stays, for announcements. Example audit, illustrative. Logos belong to their owners.

Make four lists in one sheet:


- Tools: WhatsApp or Telegram groups, Google Forms, UPI ID or QR, Zoom or Meet, Drive folders, YouTube playlists, any Excel or notebook you track fees in.

- Content: recorded classes, PDFs, PYQs, test papers, formula sheets, voice notes worth keeping. Mark each one keep, redo or drop.

- Students: name, phone, batch, what they paid for and until when.

- Dues: who owes what today, so nobody is surprised after the move.


The student list is the one to get right. Every promise you made ("this fee covers until March") must still be true after the move.






## Step 2: Set up your online academy

An online academy is your own website (and optionally your own app) where students buy your courses, watch lessons, download notes, take tests and join live classes under your name. Setting one up today takes hours, not months.

If the idea is new to you, our explainer on what an online academy is covers the options. On AllCoaching the path is fixed and self-serve: sign up, choose a plan, upload your course, connect your domain and start selling. Payments, student access, apps and hosting run on their own. Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial with no card needed, which is enough time to build the academy and test it with a few students before you announce anything.


- Name and brand: use the name students already know, the one on your WhatsApp group or YouTube channel. Add your logo and colours.

- Domain: connect your own domain (youracademy.in) so the link you share looks like yours. Every AllCoaching plan includes connecting your own domain.

- App: every plan includes your own white-label Android app; the iOS app is on Pro. Students who prefer the browser can skip the app entirely.







## Step 3: Upload your old WhatsApp content as one organised course

Do not copy your Drive folder as it is. Rebuild it as a course: modules that follow the syllabus, lessons in teaching order, a PDF of notes and a test for each module, and lesson 1 free as a demo. The structure is what a late joiner was missing on WhatsApp.



### Sort before you upload

Group your recorded classes by topic, not by date. A two-hour live class recording from last year is often better split into three or four shorter lessons. Rename files the way students search: "Module 2 · Lesson 3 · Percentage shortcuts", not "class 14 final final.mp4". Our guide on how to create your first online course in India covers module structure, lesson length and PDFs in detail.



### Videos via YouTube

Many educators already have class recordings on YouTube. On AllCoaching, videos come in through YouTube and are unlimited on every plan, so you add each lesson to the course in order instead of posting links into a chat. PDFs and test series sit in the studio's Content section, inside the same course.



### Live classes inside the course

Instead of pasting a Zoom link into the group every evening, schedule the live class inside the course. AllCoaching includes unlimited live classes on every plan, through YouTube Live, Zoom or the built-in live room. If you teach from a phone, see how to conduct live classes on mobile.


Question educators ask



### Do I have to upload everything before I switch?

No. Upload the current module, the notes students use most and the demo lesson first. Add older material module by module after the switch-over. Students care far more that this week's class and notes are in the academy than that everything from last year is.







## Step 4: How do you collect fees online for coaching instead of UPI screenshots?

Set a price on the course and let students pay through UPI or card checkout on your academy; access opens after the payment, so there is no screenshot to check and no one to add by hand. UPI is the system students already use, run by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).4



The same payment, without the evening of checking. Illustrative.



### Price the course the way you price the batch

Start with the fee students already pay you, for the same duration and the same material. A move is not the moment to change your price and your platform at once. If the academy adds recorded lessons, tests and notes that the WhatsApp batch never had, you can review the price for the next batch. Our guide on how to price online courses in India covers that decision.



### Test one real payment first

Before you announce anything, ask a friend or family member to buy the course with UPI. Check that the payment goes through, that access opens and that the confirmation makes sense to a student. On AllCoaching, students pay through UPI or card checkout and payouts reach your bank automatically through Razorpay. For the details of gateways, KYC and fees, read how to accept UPI payments for online courses.



### Students who already paid

Do not charge a student twice. Students who paid you on UPI for the current batch keep what they paid for. Decide how you will give them access before you announce; if you are not sure how to do it in your setup, ask during your trial. Many educators simply let the current batch finish its paid period and move every new enrolment and renewal to checkout.






## Step 5: Invite your existing students (message templates)

Send one clear announcement to the group about two weeks before the switch-over date, then short personal messages to anyone who has not moved. Every message needs one date, one link, what changes, what stays and a way to ask questions.



A good announcement is short and specific. Sample batch and dates. Logos belong to their owners.

Copy these and change the names, dates and link. They are written in plain English for Indian students and parents; translate them into your teaching language if your batch reads Hindi or a regional language more comfortably.


Template 1 · Group announcement

Hello everyone. From 1 December, our SSC Maths batch moves to our own academy: youracademy.in. What changes: fees are paid by UPI or card on the course page, and all lessons, PDFs, tests and the live class link are in one place, including everything from earlier months. What stays: this group, for reminders and quick updates. If you have already paid for November, you keep your access. Questions? Reply here or message me directly.



Template 2 · Reminder, three days before

Reminder: from Monday, the live class link and new notes will be only on youracademy.in. Please open the link today, sign in, and check that you can see Module 1. If something does not work, send me a message and I will help you before Monday.



Template 3 · Personal follow-up

Hi Riya, I noticed you have not signed in to the new academy yet. Everything from our batch is there now, including the PDFs you asked for last week. Here is the link: youracademy.in. Do you want me to call for two minutes and help you set it up?



Template 4 · Reply to a new enquiry

Thank you for asking about the batch. You can see the syllabus, watch a free demo lesson and enrol here: youracademy.in. Payment is by UPI or card, and access opens straight after. Class reminders are shared in our WhatsApp group, which I will add you to once you have enrolled.


For parents of school students, send the announcement to the parent as well. Parents pay the fee, and a clear message about where the money goes builds more trust than a UPI ID in a chat.






## Step 6: Keep WhatsApp as your announcement channel

Do not delete the group. Turn it into an announcement space for class reminders, new lesson alerts and exam dates, and keep fees, lessons, notes, tests and live links in the academy. WhatsApp is still where your students reply fastest.



Move the teaching and the money. Keep the chat. Logos belong to their owners.

You have three options on WhatsApp:


- Keep the group, and change its settings so only admins can send messages. Students still see every reminder; the chat stops burying your posts.

- Use a Community if you run several batches, with one announcement group for all of them.

- Start a WhatsApp Channel for public updates and free tips that bring new students in. WhatsApp says that as a channel admin "your phone number and profile photo won't be shown to followers", and that following a channel "won't reveal your phone number to the admin or other followers".3 That solves the phone-number problem for your public audience.


Our guide on WhatsApp Channels for coaching educators in India covers setting one up and what to post. Whichever you choose, every message should end with a link back to your academy, because the academy is where the student acts.






## Step 7: Set a switch-over date and keep it

Choose one date after which new fees, new notes and live class links are only in the academy, announce it about two weeks ahead, and keep it. A date turns "we are moving sometime" into something students act on.



Work back from the switch-over date. Timing is illustrative; a small batch can move in two weeks.


- Pick a natural break: the start of a new month, a new module or a new batch. Avoid the week before an exam.

- Run both for a short overlap: for the last week before the date, post new material in both places with a note that the group copy stops on the date.

- On the date, stop posting files in the group. Post the reminder and the link instead. If you keep sharing PDFs in the chat "just this once", students learn that they never need to move.







## Step 8: Follow up with students who have not moved

After the switch-over date, check your student list in the academy against your audit sheet and message every student who has not signed in, one by one. Most students who have not moved are confused, not unwilling.

The common reasons are simple: they missed the announcement, the link opened in an in-app browser, they forgot which phone number they used, or a parent pays and has not seen the message. A two-minute call fixes most of them. Educators we work with often find that the last few students move only after a personal message, not a group reminder.

After the first month, check three things: fees arrive without screenshots, late joiners find old notes on their own, and fewer questions reach your personal chat. If all three hold, the move worked.






## Does the same plan work for moving from Telegram to a course platform?

Yes. A Telegram group or channel has the same gaps as WhatsApp for a paid course: no checkout, no structured course and files that can be forwarded, so the same eight steps apply. The only difference is the announcement channel you keep.

Telegram is popular with exam educators because channels hold large audiences and large files. That is useful for free content and announcements. It is weaker for paid content, because anyone in the channel can forward a PDF out of it. Move the paid course, test series and live classes to your academy, and keep the channel for free tips and links. If you are following the news about Telegram access for educators and students in India, our update on the Telegram ban and what it means for educators explains the situation and why owning your student list matters.

## Common mistakes when moving a WhatsApp batch online

The most common mistakes are moving overnight, charging students who already paid, deleting the group, uploading a messy Drive folder as it is, never setting a switch-over date and not following up. Each has a simple fix.



Six mistakes and their fixes.


"The batch does not move because the academy is better. It moves because the educator gives one date, one link and a personal message to every student who needs it."

Amit Ratan, Founder & CEO, AllCoaching






## Glossary


Online academy
An educator's own website, and optionally app, where students buy courses, watch lessons, download notes, take tests and join live classes under the educator's brand.
Switch-over date
The fixed day after which new fees, notes and live class links are shared only in the academy, not in the WhatsApp group.
Announcement group
A WhatsApp group set so that only admins can send messages, used for reminders and alerts rather than discussion.
WhatsApp Channel
A one-way broadcast tool on WhatsApp where admins post updates to followers, and phone numbers are not shown between admins and followers.
UPI checkout
A payment step on a course page where the student pays through UPI or card and course access opens after the payment succeeds.
Anyone with the link
A sharing setting, used by Google Drive, under which anyone who has the URL can open the file, including people it was forwarded to.
Unlisted video
A YouTube video that does not appear in search or on the channel page but can be watched and shared by anyone with the link.
Migration audit
A list of every tool, piece of content, student and payment a batch uses, made before moving it to an academy.

# How to Accept UPI Payments for Online Courses in India

**Summary:** Accept UPI payments for online courses in 8 steps: pick a payment route, finish PAN and bank KYC, link checkout to course access and test it on a student&#x27;s phone.

Start your online academy today. 7 days free.

Start free trial


To accept UPI payment for online courses, you need three things: a payment route that verifies each payment, a KYC-approved account that pays out to your bank, and a link between that payment and the student's course access. The simplest reliable setup is a checkout on your own course page, run through a payment gateway such as Razorpay, that opens the course the moment UPI confirms.

Most educators start differently. You teach SSC maths in Hindi on YouTube, students message you on WhatsApp, and you send a UPI QR code. It works for ten students. At fifty, you are matching screenshots to bank entries at midnight and adding people to groups by hand.

This guide is the how-to. To compare gateways and their charges side by side, read our UPI payment gateway comparison for online courses.






## Key takeaways


- There are three ways to collect UPI for a course: a personal UPI QR, a gateway payment link, or a checkout built into your academy. Only the last one opens course access on its own.

- Bank-to-bank UPI has zero MDR, but gateways charge a platform fee. Razorpay's standard rate is 2% plus 18% GST on that fee, with ₹0 setup and ₹0 maintenance (checked October 2026).

- An individual educator can complete Razorpay KYC with a personal PAN and a bank account with IFSC, verified through CKYC or DigiLocker, with video KYC as the fallback.

- UPI has transaction limits. RBI described the general cap as ₹1 lakh per transaction and proposed ₹5 lakh for payments to hospitals and educational institutions in December 2023; very high fees may need instalments or cards.

- Test every checkout from a budget Android phone on mobile data before you announce a batch, because that is how many of your students will pay.

- On AllCoaching, UPI and card checkout is part of every plan, payouts reach your bank automatically through Razorpay, and you keep 90% of each sale on Starter or 100% on Growth and Pro.







## What does accepting UPI payments for online courses mean?

Accepting UPI payment for online courses means a student pays your course fee from any UPI app, such as Google Pay, PhonePe or Paytm, and the money reaches your bank account with a record that links the payment to that student and that course. UPI moves the money; a payment gateway or platform verifies it and settles it to you.

Three parties are involved, and it helps to keep them apart:


- UPI is the real-time bank-to-bank network run by NPCI.

- The payment gateway (also called a payment aggregator) is the company that accepts payments on your behalf, confirms them and settles the money to your bank. Razorpay, for example, describes itself as an RBI-authorised payment aggregator.[1]

- Your course platform is where the student actually buys: your website, app or academy. It decides what happens after payment, such as opening the course.




Four steps from a student's UPI app to your bank account. The third step is where course access should open.







## 3 ways to accept UPI payment for online courses

You can collect UPI for a course through a personal UPI QR, a gateway payment link, or a checkout built into your academy. They differ less in how the student pays and more in what happens after.



### 1. A personal UPI ID or QR code

You share your UPI QR on WhatsApp, the student pays and sends a screenshot. Nothing to set up, which is why almost everyone starts here. The cost is your time: you check every payment, add each student by hand, and course money mixes with household money.



### 2. A gateway payment link

After KYC with a gateway, you create a payment link for each course and share it. Razorpay states that its Payment Links let you accept payments without a website or app.[6] Every payment is verified and recorded, and students can pay by UPI or card. Course access, though, is still a separate job you do by hand.



### 3. Checkout inside your own academy

The student pays on your course page or app, and the platform enrols them once the payment is confirmed. This is how online shops work, and it grows with you.



The difference is what happens after the student pays.

When we talk to educators who move to AllCoaching, the setup we hear about most often is the first one: a UPI QR in a WhatsApp group and a notebook of who paid. It simply grew one batch at a time.






## What do you need before you accept UPI payments?

Before a gateway can pay you, it must verify who you are and which bank account is yours. This is know-your-customer (KYC) checking. Keep these ready before you sign up.



For an individual without a registered business, based on Razorpay's KYC documentation.

For an individual or unregistered business, Razorpay's documentation lists:[2]


- Proof of identity and address, auto-fetched from your Central KYC (CKYC) record. If that fails, you share Aadhaar details through DigiLocker or upload a photo ID.

- Bank details: account number and IFSC are mandatory. If the bank check fails, you are asked for proof such as a video of a cancelled cheque.

- Your personal PAN, which Razorpay uses to look up your details.[3]


A GSTIN is not always needed. Razorpay's setup flow has an "I don't have a GSTIN" option.[3] If you run a registered proprietorship, the list grows: Razorpay asks for two business proofs, such as a GST certificate, Udyam (MSME) certificate or shop and establishment certificate.[2]


Question educators ask



### Can I use my savings account for course payments?

Gateways ask for an account in your or your business's name and verify it with a small test deposit. A separate account only for course fees makes tax work easier at year end; ask your CA which type suits you.







## How to accept UPI payments for online courses: 8 steps

Here is the full setup, in the order that avoids rework. Most educators can finish it in a few days, and much of that is waiting for KYC.


- Choose how students will payPick one route: a personal UPI QR, a gateway payment link, or checkout built into your academy. For a course you will sell for months, choose a checkout that is linked to course access.

- Keep your KYC documents readyHave your personal PAN, a bank account with IFSC in your name, the mobile number linked to your Aadhaar, your course page link, and your GSTIN only if you have one.

- Complete KYC with your gateway or platformSign up, choose registered or unregistered business, confirm your PAN, finish the CKYC or DigiLocker check, and add your bank account for the small verification deposit.

- Price each course in rupeesSet one clear price per course or batch, decide whether GST is included, and show the price, contents and validity on the course page.

- Connect payment to course accessMake sure a confirmed payment enrols the student in the right course automatically, so you never add students by hand.

- Write a refund and support policyPublish a short refund policy and one support contact before the first sale, so payment questions have a clear answer.

- Test with a real paymentBuy your own course from a budget Android phone on mobile data with two or three UPI apps, then check the record, the access and the confirmation message.

- Share the course link and reconcile monthlyPut one course link in YouTube, WhatsApp and Instagram, then match payouts in your bank to sales once a month and export the records.




### Step 5 in detail: connect payment to access

If a payment does not enrol the student automatically, every sale becomes a manual task: find the payment, find the student, add them, send the link. With built-in checkout, the payment confirmation itself opens the course. Our guide on automating student onboarding covers what should happen in the minutes after a payment.



### Step 7 in detail: test like a student

Buy your own course from a budget Android phone on mobile data, not from your laptop on office Wi-Fi. Try Google Pay, then PhonePe, then Paytm. Check that the payment shows in your records, the course opens, and the confirmation reads well in your students' language, whether that is a Hindi-medium NEET batch or a spoken-English class for working adults.

## How much does it cost to accept UPI payments for courses?

UPI itself costs the merchant nothing on bank-to-bank payments, but the gateway that verifies and settles the payment charges a platform fee. On Razorpay's standard pricing, that fee is 2% of each payment plus 18% GST on the fee, with no setup fee and no yearly maintenance charge.[1]

Razorpay's own pricing page explains the split: there is zero MDR (merchant discount rate) on standard bank-to-bank UPI, "however, a standard platform or technology fee of 2% will be applied" for its dashboard, reporting and infrastructure.[1] Cashfree lists a platform fee from 1.95% on its standard payment modes and says it charges zero setup fees.[5] Rates change, so check the live page before you sign up.

For one illustrative ₹1,999 course sold by UPI on that standard rate, the fee is ₹39.98 plus ₹7.20 GST, and ₹1,951.82 is settled to you. Income tax and any GST on your own course fee are separate.



Illustrative. Razorpay's standard rates, checked October 2026.

A gateway on its own gives you payments, not a website, an app or course delivery. If you use a course platform, add its price too. On AllCoaching, Growth (₹7,999 a month) and Pro (₹14,999 a month) take 0% commission, so you keep 100% of every sale, with no lock-in; Starter is ₹6,999 a year with a 10% platform fee on sales; details are on the pricing page. All prices exclude GST, and payment-gateway charges on student payments are separate. To choose a price students will actually pay, read how to price online courses in India.






## Is there a UPI limit on course fees?

Yes. UPI has per-transaction limits, so a very high course fee may not go through in a single UPI payment. In December 2023, the Reserve Bank of India said the UPI transaction limit was capped at ₹1 lakh, except for a few categories, and proposed raising the limit for payments to hospitals and educational institutions to ₹5 lakh per transaction.[4]


"To encourage the use of UPI for medical and educational services, it is proposed to enhance the limit for payments to hospitals and educational institutions from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh per transaction."

Reserve Bank of India, Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies, 8 December 2023

Whether the higher limit applies to your academy depends on how your gateway classifies your business, so ask your gateway rather than assume it. Most SSC courses, UPSC test series or yoga programmes cost far less than ₹1 lakh. For an expensive year-long programme, offer instalments or card and net banking alongside UPI.






## Do you need GST registration to accept UPI payments?

Not always to start. Razorpay's sign-up flow lets eligible applicants continue without a GSTIN.[3] Whether you must register for GST, and whether GST applies to your course fees, is a tax question that depends on your turnover and how you teach, not on the payment method.

Decide before launch whether your listed price includes GST and say so on the course page. Note that the 18% GST in the fee maths above is charged on the gateway's fee, not on your course price.[1] For the rules on coaching fees, read our guides on GST for coaching institutes and GST and income tax for online tutors, and confirm your case with a chartered accountant.






## How to make UPI checkout work on students' phones

A UPI checkout works best when it takes one tap from the course page, opens the student's UPI app directly, and confirms access on the same screen. Most of your students will pay on a phone, often a budget Android phone on mobile data, so design for that first.


- Share a course page link, not a QR image. A student cannot scan a QR on the phone they are paying from.

- Show the price, what is included and the validity before the pay button. "₹1,999 · 120 lessons · Hindi medium · valid till the 2026 exam" answers the questions that otherwise arrive on WhatsApp.

- Keep the page light. A heavy page on a slow connection loses students. Our course landing page guide covers the layout.

- Write confirmation messages in your teaching language. A Hindi-medium student should see what to do next in Hindi or simple English.

- Put the link where students already are. YouTube descriptions, a pinned WhatsApp message, your Instagram bio. If students are reluctant to install an app, see what to do when students won't download your app.




Moving from screenshots on WhatsApp to a checkout that confirms itself. Logos belong to their owners.






## Common UPI payment mistakes course sellers make

The most common mistake is treating a payment screenshot as proof of payment. Screenshots can be old or edited, and checking each one does not scale. Use payments your gateway has verified.



Five habits that cost time, and the fix for each.




#### Do

Collect through a gateway or platform checkout. Keep a separate bank account for course fees. Publish a short refund policy before the batch starts. Share one course link everywhere. Test on a budget phone before every launch.



#### Avoid

Accepting screenshots as proof. Mixing fees with personal spending. Deciding refunds case by case on WhatsApp. Posting a QR image as your only way to pay. Launching a batch without a test payment.


One more: do not leave payment records only inside a chat app. When a parent asks for a receipt in March, or your CA asks for a year of sales, you want a record you can export.

## Glossary


UPI (Unified Payments Interface)
India's real-time bank-to-bank payment network run by NPCI, used through apps such as Google Pay, PhonePe and Paytm.
Payment gateway
A company that accepts online payments for a business, verifies each one and settles the money to the business's bank account. Razorpay, for example, is authorised by the RBI as a payment aggregator.
MDR (merchant discount rate)
The charge a merchant's bank takes on a digital payment. Bank-to-bank UPI and RuPay debit card payments carry zero MDR.
Platform fee
A percentage a gateway or course platform keeps from each payment for its service. It is separate from MDR and usually attracts GST.
KYC (know your customer)
The identity and bank-account checks a payment company must complete before it can pay money out to you.
CKYC (Central KYC)
A central registry of verified KYC records, maintained by CERSAI, that payment companies can look up with your PAN, so you upload fewer documents.
Settlement
The transfer of collected payments, minus fees, from the gateway to your bank account on the gateway's settlement cycle.






## Frequently asked questions

Can I accept UPI payments for online courses without a website?Yes. You can use a personal QR code or a gateway payment link; Razorpay says its Payment Links work without a website or app. Course access then stays manual, so a checkout on your own course page saves time as you grow.

Is UPI free for course sellers in India?Bank-to-bank UPI carries zero MDR, but payment gateways charge a platform fee for verifying and settling payments. Razorpay's standard rate is 2% plus 18% GST on that fee, with no setup or maintenance charge (checked October 2026).

What documents do I need to accept UPI payments as an individual tutor?For an individual without a registered business, Razorpay asks for your personal PAN and a bank account number with IFSC; identity and address are fetched from your CKYC record, with DigiLocker, a photo ID upload or video KYC as fallbacks. A GSTIN is needed only if you have one.

Do I need GST registration to accept UPI payments for my courses?Not to start on Razorpay, which offers a route for eligible applicants without a GSTIN. Whether you must register for GST, and whether GST applies to your course fees, depends on your turnover and situation, so confirm it with a chartered accountant.

Is there a maximum amount a student can pay by UPI for a course?Yes. In December 2023 the RBI said the general UPI limit was ₹1 lakh per transaction and proposed ₹5 lakh for payments to hospitals and educational institutions. For higher fees, offer instalments or let students pay by card or net banking.

Is it safe to collect course fees on my personal UPI ID?It works for a few students, but screenshots can be edited, each student is added by hand, and course money mixes with personal money. A gateway or platform checkout gives verified records and can open access automatically.

How do students pay by UPI on AllCoaching?Students pay with UPI or a card on your own academy website or app, course access opens after payment, and payouts reach your bank automatically through Razorpay. # How to Create an Online Course in India (2026 Guide)

**Source:** https://allcoaching.in/blog/create-your-first-online-course-india  
**Published:** 2026-10-25T09:00:00+05:30  
**Updated:** 2026-10-27T09:00:00+05:30  
**Author:** Amit Ratan, Founder &amp; CEO, AllCoaching  

**Summary:** How to create an online course in India: pick one outcome, plan modules of 5–15 minute lessons, record on a phone budget, add PDF notes and tests, then pilot it.

Amit RatanUpdated 27 Oct 2026 · 21 min read


On this page


Start your online academy today. 7 days free.

Start free trial


To create an online course in India, choose one clear outcome for one group of students, split the syllabus into modules of 5–15 minute lessons, record them on your phone with a clip-on mic, add PDF notes and a test to every module, offer one free demo lesson, and test the whole course with 5–10 students before you sell it. You do not need a studio, an editor or a developer to do any of this.

Maybe you teach NEET biology to a batch of thirty in Kota or Patna and want students from other cities to learn from you. Maybe you teach SSC maths in Hindi on YouTube, spoken English to working adults on Zoom, yoga to a morning group, or classical vocal music on weekends. You already know how to teach. What feels new is turning that teaching into a course: something a student can buy, open on a phone and finish without you in the room.

This guide covers the whole build, in order: picking the topic and outcome, structuring modules and lessons, choosing between video, PDF, tests and live classes, a recording setup on a budget, teaching on camera, editing with free tools, Hindi and regional medium with captions, the free demo lesson, uploading and organising everything in your academy, the pilot batch and how to keep the course up to date. If you have not set up an academy yet, read how to start an online academy in 5 steps alongside this; that guide covers sign-up, domain and payments, and this one goes deep on the course itself.






## Key takeaways


- Start from one outcome, such as "score 300+ in NEET biology" or "speak confidently in a job interview", not from a list of topics.

- Structure the course like a syllabus: 4–8 modules, each made of 5–15 minute video lessons with one idea each, a PDF of notes and a module test.

- Audio matters more than the camera. A phone you already own plus a lapel mic (illustratively ₹500–₹2,000) is enough for a first course.

- Use free tools: OBS Studio records the screen, Shotcut edits video, and YouTube automatic captions support Hindi; review every caption before students see it.

- Host lessons on YouTube as unlisted videos, which only people with the link can watch, and keep a public free lesson on your channel to bring students in.

- Pilot with 5–10 students before launch and fix the top three problems they find.

- On AllCoaching, videos via YouTube and live classes are unlimited on every plan, with PDF notes and test series in the same course, after a 7-day free trial with no card.







## How to create an online course in India: the 8 steps

Choose an outcome, outline modules and lessons, pick your formats, set up a budget recording kit, script and record, edit and caption, upload and organise in your academy, then pilot with a small batch. Every section below expands one of these steps.


- Choose the topic and outcomePick a topic you already teach and write one sentence naming the student, the result and the time the course takes.

- Outline modules and lessonsSplit the syllabus into 4–8 modules and each module into 5–15 minute lessons that teach one idea each.

- Pick your formatsPlan video lessons to teach, a PDF of notes and a test for every module, and a weekly live class for doubts.

- Set up a budget recording kitUse your phone, a lapel mic, a tripod and soft light facing you, plus a free screen recorder for slides and problems.

- Script and recordWrite a bullet outline per lesson (hook, idea, examples, practice, recap) and record one module at a time.

- Edit and captionTrim mistakes and pauses with a free editor, export MP4, and review YouTube automatic captions in Hindi or English.

- Upload and organise in your academyUpload videos to YouTube as unlisted, add them to the course in order with PDFs and tests, and mark lesson 1 as a free demo.

- Pilot with 5–10 studentsOpen module 1 to a small batch, collect where they get stuck, fix the top three issues and then launch to everyone.


Most first courses take longer than planned for one reason: the educator records first and plans later. Two weeks of recording later, the lessons are 70 minutes long, out of order, and there is no test anywhere. Planning on paper for one evening saves weeks of re-recording.

When educators build a first course with us, the ones who launch fastest are rarely the ones with the best camera. They are the ones who wrote the module list first, recorded one module at a time, and opened the course to a few students before it felt finished.






## How do you choose the topic and outcome for your first online course?

Choose a topic you have already taught to real students, and write the outcome as one sentence a student would say after finishing the course. The outcome decides what goes in and, more importantly, what stays out.



### Start from what you already teach

Your first course should be the one you could teach tomorrow without preparing: the chapter you have explained a hundred times, the batch you run every year, the skill students already ask you about. You know where students get stuck, which examples work and which questions come up. That experience is what a student is paying for.



### Write the outcome, not the topic

"Biology" is a subject. "NEET biology" is a topic. "Finish the Class 11 human physiology syllabus with chapter tests, in Hindi, in six weeks" is an outcome. Write yours as one sentence that names the student, the result and the time:


- Exam: "SSC CGL aspirants can solve arithmetic questions in under a minute each, in 30 days."

- Exam: "NEET droppers revise the full plant physiology unit with 300 practice questions."

- Skill: "Freshers can answer the ten most common interview questions in clear English."

- Skill: "Beginners can follow a 20-minute morning yoga routine safely at home."

- Skill: "Students can sing five basic ragas with correct sargam."


A sharp outcome makes every later choice easier. If a lesson does not move the student toward it, it goes in a later course. It also gives you the course title and the first line of its description, and it helps you price the online course against what students already pay for that result.


Question educators ask



### Should my first course be big or small?

Small. A focused course of 20 to 40 short lessons that you can finish recording in two to four weeks beats a 200-lesson "complete" course that never launches. You can add a second course, a test series or a live batch once the first one sells.







## What is a good course structure for an online course?

A good online course structure is a course split into 4–8 modules, each module made of short video lessons of 5–15 minutes with one idea each, followed by a PDF of notes and a module test. Students should always know where they are and what comes next.



One course, four modules, short lessons. Example structure, illustrative.



### Modules follow the syllabus

For an exam course, your modules are usually the units of the official syllabus in the order you teach them: number system, percentage, ratio, algebra for SSC maths; cell biology, plant physiology, human physiology for NEET biology. For a skill course, modules follow the order a learner can handle: breathing and posture before asanas, sounds before sentences in spoken English, sargam before ragas.



### Lessons of 5–15 minutes

A recorded lesson is not a classroom period. In a 60-minute class you repeat, take questions and wait for the slowest student; on video, a student can pause and replay. Cut each topic into lessons of one idea each. Most land between 5 and 15 minutes. Short lessons are easier to watch on a phone during a commute, easier to find when revising, and much easier to re-record when something changes.



### Write the outline before you record

Put the outline in a simple sheet: module, lesson number, lesson title, the one idea it teaches, its length target, the PDF that goes with it, and the test questions it feeds. If you want help drafting the first version from your syllabus, our guide to using ChatGPT for course curriculum design shows how, but always edit the draft with your own teaching order.



CourseModulesLessons (illustrative)Per module

NEET biology, Hindi medium6 units45–60 lessons of 10–15 minNotes PDF, diagram sheet, 30-question test
SSC CGL maths8 topics50–70 lessons of 6–12 minFormula PDF, practice set, timed test
Spoken English for interviews5 stages25–35 lessons of 5–10 minPhrase sheet PDF, speaking task, quiz
Morning yoga for beginners4 weeks20–28 lessons of 8–20 minRoutine PDF, safety notes, check-in quiz

Example course structures. Numbers are illustrative; shape yours around your own syllabus.







## Videos, PDFs, tests and live classes: which formats does your course need?

Most Indian online courses work best with four formats together: video lessons to teach, PDF notes to revise, tests to check what stuck, and live classes to answer doubts. Video alone is a playlist; the other three turn it into a course.



Each format has one job. Logos belong to their owners.



### Video lessons

Videos carry the teaching. Many Indian educators host lesson videos on YouTube and keep them unlisted. YouTube's help centre says unlisted videos "can be seen and shared by anyone with the link" and won't show up in YouTube's search results unless someone adds them to a public playlist; they also do not appear on your channel's Videos tab.1 That makes them a practical way to host paid lessons, with one caution: anyone who has the link can share it, so treat unlisted as private-ish, not secret.



### PDF notes

Students revise from notes, not from replaying a video. Give each module a PDF: chapter notes, labelled diagrams, a formula sheet, previous-year questions or, for skills, a routine or phrase sheet. Make them readable on a 6-inch phone screen: large text, one column, and headings that match the lesson titles.



### Tests and quizzes

Tests tell the student, and you, whether the lessons worked. Use a short quiz after each module and, for exam courses, full-length timed mock tests at the end. Our guide to creating interactive mock tests online covers question types, timing and solutions in detail.



### Live classes

A weekly live doubt class makes a recorded course feel taught, not just sold. It is also where you hear the questions that become your next lessons. If you teach from a phone, see how to conduct live classes on mobile for the setup.

On AllCoaching, a course holds all four in one place: videos added through YouTube, PDF notes and test series in the studio's Content section, and live classes through YouTube Live, Zoom or the built-in live room. Videos via YouTube and live classes are unlimited on every plan, so the format mix is a teaching decision, not a cost decision.






## What is a good online course recording setup in India on a budget?

A good budget recording setup is the smartphone you already own, a lapel (clip-on) mic, a tripod or phone stand, soft light facing you, and a free screen recorder for slides or problem-solving. Students forgive an average picture; they do not forgive audio they cannot hear.



Start with the mic. Price ranges are illustrative (India, October 2026) and vary by model and seller.



### Sound first: the lapel mic

A phone's built-in mic picks up the fan, the traffic and the echo of a bare room. A wired or wireless lapel mic clipped 15–20 cm below your chin fixes most of that. Illustratively, these cost ₹500–₹2,000 in India. Record in the quietest room you have; curtains, a bed and a bookshelf absorb echo better than any foam panel.



### A steady frame at eye level

Mount the phone on a tripod or stand (illustratively ₹400–₹1,500) at eye level, about an arm and a half away. Record horizontally. YouTube's recommended upload settings note that "the standard aspect ratio for YouTube on a computer is 16:9" and list MP4 as the recommended container,3 which is what a phone in landscape mode already records.



### Light facing you

Sit facing a window during the day, or use a ring light or soft lamp (illustratively ₹800–₹2,500) behind the phone. Avoid a window behind you; it turns your face into a silhouette.



### Screen recording and a writing surface

Maths, physics and accounts students need to see you solve. Two cheap ways: record your screen while you write on slides or a digital whiteboard, or mount the phone over a notebook and write with a thick pen. OBS Studio describes itself as "free and open source software for video recording and live streaming"4 and works on Windows, Mac and Linux. A pen tablet (illustratively ₹3,000–₹15,000 depending on size) is a later upgrade, not a requirement. For a wider tool list, see our guide to the best free tools for teachers to record lectures.




#### Do

Buy a mic first. Record a 30-second test and listen on cheap earphones. Turn on airplane mode while recording. Keep the same spot, light and framing for the whole course so lessons look consistent.



#### Avoid

Buying a camera before you have recorded a single lesson. Recording next to a ceiling fan or an open window. Switching between portrait and landscape across lessons. Using the phone's front camera when the rear one is much sharper.







## How do you script and teach on camera?

Script each lesson as a bullet outline, not a word-for-word text: a hook, the one idea, two examples, a practice question and a recap. Then teach to one imagined student, the way you would at your desk.



One idea per lesson. Timings are illustrative.



### The five-part lesson


- Hook (under a minute): show an exam question or real situation the student cannot handle yet.

- Teach: the one idea, step by step, with the board or slide on screen.

- Examples: two solved examples, an easy one then an exam-level one.

- Practice: "pause the video and try this one", then show the answer.

- Recap: three lines, and what the next lesson covers.




### Talking to a lens

Most educators find the first ten recordings awkward and the next ten normal. A few things help: stick a small note with the student's name you are teaching to next to the lens; keep your bullet outline just below the camera; record each lesson in one or two takes and accept small slips; and stand or sit the way you do in class, not stiffly. Students choose a teacher for clarity and warmth, not for a newsreader's polish.



### Batch your recording

Record a whole module in one or two sittings: same clothes, same light, same framing. It is faster, and the module looks like one piece. Label files as you go (M2-L04-percentage-shortcuts.mp4) so editing and uploading stay in order.


"The educators whose first courses sell are not the best performers on camera. They are the ones whose lessons are short, in order and clearly explained."

Amit Ratan, Founder & CEO, AllCoaching






## How should you edit course videos with free tools?

Edit lightly: trim the start and end, cut long pauses and mistakes, raise the volume if needed, and add a title card. Course students want clarity, not transitions and music.

Free editors are enough for this. Shotcut, for example, describes itself as "a free, open source, cross-platform video editor".5 On a phone, the built-in gallery trimmer handles start and end cuts. If you made a mistake while recording, pause for two seconds, then repeat the sentence; the pause makes the cut easy to find later.


- Keep: trims, cuts of long silences, a simple title card with module and lesson number, on-screen text for formulas or key words.

- Skip: background music under speech, fancy transitions, zoom effects on every sentence, intros longer than five seconds.

- Export: MP4 in landscape at the resolution you recorded. YouTube lists MP4 as its recommended container.3


A useful rule: if a lesson needs more than 15 minutes of editing, re-record it instead. Over-editing is the most common reason a first course takes months instead of weeks.






## Should you create an online course in Hindi or a regional language?

Teach in the language your students think in and search in. For many Indian exam and skill students that is Hindi, Hinglish or a regional language, not English, and a course in their medium often feels made for them.



Choose the medium, then caption it. Logos belong to their owners.



### Pick one medium per course

Decide the medium before you record, and say it in the course title: "NEET Biology in Hindi", "SSC Maths in Hinglish", "MPSC Polity in Marathi". Mixing languages lesson by lesson confuses students. If you plan to serve two mediums, record two courses; the outline and PDFs can be shared and translated.



### Technical terms

Exam students in Hindi medium still meet English terms in many papers and textbooks. A common approach is to teach in Hindi while writing key terms in both scripts on the board ("कोशिका / cell") and keeping a bilingual glossary in the module PDF.



### Captions

Captions help students in noisy hostels, students with hearing loss and students revising quickly. YouTube creates automatic captions using speech recognition, and Hindi is among its supported languages. Its help page is clear about the limits:2


"Always review automatic captions and edit any parts that haven't been properly transcribed."

YouTube Help, "Use automatic captioning"

In practice, review the names, formulas and subject terms first; those are what automatic captions get wrong most. Captions are a YouTube feature, so check how they appear in your academy's player during your pilot.






## Why does every online course need a free demo lesson?

A free demo lesson lets students judge your teaching before they pay, and it is usually the single most persuasive thing on your course page. Make lesson 1 free and make it genuinely useful.



An example path for a spoken English course. Illustrative. Logos belong to their owners.


- Teach one thing fully. A demo that only lists what the course covers sells nothing. A demo that solves a real problem sells the next lesson.

- Keep it 10–15 minutes, recorded with the same kit and style as the rest of the course, so the student knows exactly what they are buying.

- End with the path: what the full course covers, how long it takes, and where to enrol.


Your public YouTube videos do the same job one step earlier. A useful free lesson on your channel brings a student to your academy; the demo lesson there turns that interest into a decision. When you are ready to promote the course, our guide on how to sell courses online in India picks up from here.






## How do you upload and organise your course in your academy?

Create the course, add lessons in syllabus order module by module, attach each module's PDF and test, mark lesson 1 as free, write the description from your outcome sentence, and keep the course in draft until the pilot is done.



Five steps per lesson, batched by module. Studio preview · sample data. Logos belong to their owners.



### Name things the way students search

Use titles students would type: "SSC CGL Maths in Hindi: Arithmetic Complete Course", not "Batch 7 Recorded". Number lessons consistently (Module 2 · Lesson 4 · Percentage shortcuts) so the list reads like a syllabus.



### Write the description from the outcome

The first line is your outcome sentence. Then list what is inside: number of modules, lessons, PDFs and tests, the live class schedule, the language, and who it is for and not for. That is the information students compare.

## How do you test an online course with 5–10 students before launch?

Give the course free or at a discount to 5–10 students from your current batch or audience, ask them to finish module 1 within a week on their own phones, and fix the top three problems they report before you open it to everyone.



A small pilot batch finds problems before paying students do.



### Who to pick

Choose a mix: two strong students, two average ones, one or two who struggle, and at least one who uses a basic Android phone on mobile data. If you teach a skill, include someone who has never tried it. Their confusion is your most useful data.



### What to ask


- Where did you stop watching, and why?

- Which lesson needed a second watch?

- Was the audio clear on your earphones?

- Was any test question unclear or wrong?

- What did you search for that was not in the course?


Collect the answers in one sheet and count. If three students ask the same question, it becomes a new lesson or a line in the PDF. If two students stopped at the same lesson, that lesson is too long or out of order.

Pilot students also give you your first honest feedback to quote on the course page, with their permission and in their own words. Never add results or ranks you cannot prove.






## How often should you update an online course?

Review the course after every batch and before every exam cycle: re-record lessons that confuse students, update PDFs and tests when the syllabus or pattern changes, and add lessons for questions that keep coming up in live classes. Short lessons make this cheap; you replace one 10-minute video, not a 90-minute lecture.


- After each batch: read the doubt-class questions and test results; fix the weakest three lessons.

- When an exam notification changes the pattern: update the outline, tests and the course description first, then the affected lessons.

- Every year: refresh the demo lesson and the course title year so students know it is current.


Keep a simple change log at the top of the course description ("Updated October 2026: new mock tests for the revised pattern"). Students trust a course that visibly stays current, and you avoid the trap of a second "2027 edition" that splits your students across two versions.






## Common mistakes when you create your first online course

The most common first-course mistakes are recording full-length classroom lectures, buying equipment before recording anything, reading a script, over-editing, shipping videos without notes or tests, and launching without a pilot. Each has a simple fix.



Six mistakes we see most often, and the fix for each.

One more that is easy to miss: keeping everything in WhatsApp groups and Drive links. It works for one batch, then breaks when you have three batches, two price points and students asking who has access to what. Putting the course in one place, with its own checkout, is what lets it run while you teach the next batch.






## Glossary


Course outcome
One sentence describing what a student will be able to do after finishing the course, and in how long.
Module
A group of related lessons inside a course, usually one unit or chapter of the syllabus, ending with notes and a test.
Micro-lesson
A short video lesson of about 5–15 minutes that teaches one idea.
Lapel mic
A small clip-on microphone worn on the shirt, close to the mouth, that records clearer voice than a phone's built-in mic.
Screen recording
A video capture of your computer or tablet screen, used to teach with slides, a digital whiteboard or software.
Unlisted video
A YouTube video that anyone with the link can watch but that does not appear in YouTube search or on your channel's Videos tab.
Automatic captions
Subtitles that YouTube generates from a video's speech using speech recognition, which the educator should review and correct.
Demo lesson
One complete lesson offered free so students can judge your teaching before they buy the course.
Pilot batch
A small group of 5–10 students who take a new course before launch so the educator can find and fix problems.

How do I create an online course in India?Choose one outcome for one group of students, split the syllabus into modules of 5–15 minute lessons, record them on a phone with a lapel mic, add PDF notes and a test to each module, offer a free demo lesson, upload everything to your academy and pilot it with 5–10 students before launch.

How do I make an online course on my phone?Mount the phone on a tripod in landscape at eye level, clip a lapel mic below your chin, sit facing soft light, and record one short lesson at a time. Trim the start and end in a free editor or the phone's gallery, export MP4 and upload it.

Can I create an online course in Hindi?Yes. Choose Hindi as the medium for the whole course, say so in the title, write key technical terms in both scripts, and use YouTube automatic captions, which support Hindi, after reviewing them for errors in names and subject terms.

What equipment do I need to record an online course in India?A smartphone you already own, a lapel mic, a tripod or phone stand, and soft light facing you. Illustratively a lapel mic costs ₹500–₹2,000 and a stand ₹400–₹1,500 in India. A free screen recorder such as OBS Studio covers slides and problem-solving.

How long should online course videos be?Most lessons work best at 5–15 minutes with one idea each. Short lessons are easier to watch on a phone, easier to find when revising and easier to re-record when the syllabus changes.

What is a good structure for an online course?Four to eight modules that follow the syllabus or a learning order, each made of short video lessons, one PDF of notes and a module test, with full mock tests or a final project at the end and lesson 1 free as a demo.

Where should I host my course videos?Many Indian educators upload lessons to YouTube as unlisted videos, which only people with the link can watch, and add them to a paid course in their academy. On AllCoaching, videos via YouTube are unlimited on every plan.

Should I test my course before launching it?Yes. Give it to 5–10 students free or at a discount, ask them to finish module 1 in a week on their own phones, and fix the top three problems they report before you open it to everyone.

How much does it cost to create and sell an online course in India?Recording can start with a phone you own plus a mic. To sell it from your own academy on AllCoaching, there is a 7-day free trial with no card, then Growth at ₹7,999 a month or Pro at ₹14,999 a month with 0% commission, so you keep 100% of every sale, or Starter at ₹6,999 a year with a 10% platform fee, all excluding GST.

# Meta Ads for Coaching Institutes in India (2026 Guide)

**Source:** https://allcoaching.in/blog/meta-ads-for-coaching-institutes  
**Published:** 2026-10-25T09:00:00+05:30  
**Updated:** 2026-10-27T09:00:00+05:30

**Summary:** Meta ads for a coaching institute, step by step: the right objective, audiences for exam and skill courses, Hindi reels, Pixel tracking and an illustrative budget test.

Amit RatanUpdated 27 Oct 2026 · 23 min read
