# EdTech App Fatigue: Why Students Won&#x27;t Install Your App

**Source:** https://allcoaching.in/blog/edtech-marketplace-india-app-fatigue  
**Published:** 2026-04-25T09:00:00+05:30  
**Updated:** 2026-10-27T09:00:00+05:30  
**Author:** Amit Ratan, Founder &amp; CEO, AllCoaching  

**Summary:** App fatigue is why students skip one more coaching app. Build a web-first academy on your own domain, offer an optional app, keep one login and cut your tool stack.

Amit RatanUpdated 27 Oct 2026 · 17 min read


On this page


Start your online academy today. 7 days free.

Start free trial


App fatigue is the reluctance students feel to download, sign up for and keep one more app, and in Indian online education it shows up as students who never get past your install step. The fix for an educator is not a better app pitch. It is an academy that works in the browser on your own domain first, with your own app offered to the students who want it.

Picture a Class 12 NEET student in Gaya. Her phone has 64 GB of storage, a school app, YouTube, WhatsApp, Telegram, two test-series apps and an app from a teacher she tried last year. Her monthly data pack runs out around the 20th. You send her a link to your new biology batch and the first thing it asks is to install another app. She closes it and goes back to YouTube.

This guide explains what app fatigue is, why students won't download a coaching app, what it costs you, and how to build around it: a coaching app vs website comparison, a web-first academy path, when to offer the app, how to cut the tool stack and a seven-step plan. If you are still deciding what an academy is, start with what an online academy is.






## Key takeaways


- App fatigue is real: students resist installing one more app because of low storage, data limits, shared phones, repeated sign-ups and too many alerts.

- The install step is the leak: every extra step between your link and your lesson loses some students, and an app store visit is a big step.

- Web first, app optional: let a student open your link, watch a free lesson and pay by UPI in the browser; offer your app after purchase to daily learners.

- Your own domain builds trust that an unknown app link cannot: students see your name, not a download prompt.

- Fewer tools beat more apps: move lessons, notes, tests, live classes and payments into one academy and keep WhatsApp for reminders.

- On AllCoaching: sign up, choose a plan, upload your course, connect your domain and start selling, with your own Android app on every plan and iOS on Pro, after a 7-day free trial with no card.







## What is app fatigue in online education?

App fatigue in online education is the tiredness and resistance students feel when every teacher, test series and school asks them to install a separate app, each with its own sign-up, OTP, notifications and storage cost. The result is that many students stop installing new learning apps at all, even from teachers they like.



One student, one phone, a separate app for every teacher. Illustrative.

It is easy to dismiss this as a minor annoyance. It is not, for one reason: the student decides whether to try you at the exact moment you ask for the install. If that moment feels like work, she leaves before she has seen a single minute of your teaching.



### How app fatigue shows up for an educator


- Link clicks without sign-ups. Students tap the link in your YouTube description, land on an app store page and never install.

- Installs without purchases. They install, hit a sign-up screen, and never return.

- Uninstalls after the batch. When storage runs low, your app is the first to go once the course ends, along with your next-batch announcements.

- "Sir, please send on WhatsApp." Students ask for PDFs and links on WhatsApp because that is the app they already open fifty times a day.


If the last point is your daily reality, our guide on students who won't download your app and only want WhatsApp goes deeper into that specific habit.






## Why students won't download one more coaching app

Students won't download a coaching app mainly because of low phone storage, limited data, shared family phones, low trust in an unknown app, alert overload and not yet knowing whether the teacher is worth it. None of these is about your teaching, and each has a fix that does not need the student to install anything first.



Six reasons students skip the install, and what each one asks of you.



### 1. Storage on budget phones

Many students prepare for NEET, SSC or state exams on entry-level Android phones. When storage fills up, the phone itself nudges them to delete things: Google's Android Help page on freeing up storage has a section headed "Uninstall apps you don't use".1 A coaching app that has not earned a daily habit yet is an easy candidate.



### 2. Data limits

Google says this plainly in its guidance for app developers: "Users often avoid downloading apps that seem too large, particularly in emerging markets where devices connect to spotty 2G and 3G networks or work on plans with data limits."2 A student on a daily data pack weighs every download against tonight's lecture.



### 3. Shared phones

In many homes, a younger student studies on a parent's phone or a sibling's. Installing apps on someone else's phone needs permission. Opening a link in the browser does not.



### 4. Low trust in an unknown app

A link that asks for an install from an app the student has never heard of feels risky, especially when it then asks for a phone number. A web page that clearly carries your name, photo and course on your own domain feels like the teacher they already know from YouTube.



### 5. Too many alerts

Every app on the phone competes for attention with notifications. Students who feel buried in alerts start muting or deleting apps, not adding them.



### 6. They are not sure about you yet

This is the biggest one. A student who has watched two of your YouTube videos is curious, not committed. Asking for an install before she has seen your course is asking for commitment too early. Let her try you first.






## What app fatigue costs an educator

App fatigue costs an educator enrolments at the install step, and with them part of the marketing effort that brought each student to the link. You pay for traffic, whether in reels, YouTube effort or ads, and then lose part of it before the student ever sees your course page.



Two paths from the same link. Bar widths are illustrative, not measured data.



### Lost at the install step

Think of the path from your link to a paid enrolment as a set of steps. In an app-first path the student taps your link, goes to an app store, installs, signs up with an OTP, then finds and buys the course. In a web-first path she taps the link, sees the course page, watches the free lesson, signs up and pays. Both paths have a sign-up, but only one asks for an install before the student has seen anything. Every step loses some people; the install is usually the expensive one.



### Wasted marketing spend

If you run Meta ads, the cost per click is the same whether the click ends in an app store or on your course page. Sending paid clicks to a course page that opens immediately gives each click a better chance. Our guide to Meta ads for coaching institutes covers how to measure that with the Meta Pixel.

When educators move their academy to us, the change we hear about first is rarely the website itself. It is that they can send one link and stop answering the same five questions every evening.






## Coaching app vs website: which do students actually use?

Students use both, at different moments: a website on your own domain is better for the first visit, search and sharing, and an app is better for daily learners in a long batch. So the question is not app or website. It is which one you put first.



What each does best. General comparison.

General comparison for a single educator or a small institute. On AllCoaching, your own Android app is on every plan and the iOS app on Pro.


A website also has a quiet advantage: search. Your course pages and topic pages can be found on Google by students who have never heard of you, while the screens inside an app cannot. That is why our guide to running an LMS on your own domain treats the domain as the foundation, not an extra.


Question educators ask



### Should I stop offering an app?

No. Students in a long batch, or on a daily test series, often prefer an app because it is one tap away and remembers where they stopped. Keep the app, but stop making it the front door. Let the website be the front door and offer the app inside, after the student has bought.







## The fix: a web-first academy on your own domain

A web-first academy is one where a student can go from your link to your course page, a free lesson, UPI checkout and learning entirely in the browser, on your own domain, without installing anything. The app is still there for students who want it, but nobody has to install it to start.



One link, no install. Studio preview · sample data.



### What the student sees


- Your link, for example youracademy.in/neet-biology, in your YouTube description, Instagram bio or WhatsApp message.

- Your course page with your photo, the syllabus, the language, validity, the price and a free lesson.

- UPI or card checkout on the same page. Access opens on its own once the payment goes through.

- Lessons, PDFs, tests and live classes in the browser, on any phone or laptop.




### Why the web is enough for most first visits

The browser is already installed on every phone, it does not ask for storage, and a link from a teacher the student follows feels familiar. The web has also grown up: Google's web.dev describes Progressive Web Apps as web apps that reach "any web user on any device with a single codebase".3

Your academy website runs on your own domain on every plan, students pay by UPI or card with automatic Razorpay payouts, and live classes are unlimited through YouTube Live, Zoom or the built-in live room. ## Offer your own app, but make it optional

Offer your own app after a student has bought, to the students who learn with you every day, and never make it a condition of trying you. An optional app keeps its strengths (one tap, a home-screen icon in your name) without becoming the step that loses new students.



Two groups, one academy underneath.



### Who is happy on the web

A student trying your free lesson, someone buying a short crash course, anyone on a nearly full phone and anyone studying on a family phone. For these students the browser is not a compromise. It is the easiest way in.



### Who will want your app

A student on a daily test series, someone in a year-long batch with a live class every evening, a learner who studies on the bus and anyone who simply asks for one. For them an app in your name is a convenience worth the storage, and by then they trust you.



### How to offer it without pressure


- Mention the app on the thank-you message after purchase, not on the course page.

- Say what it is for: "Daily tests are quicker in the app." Not: "Download our app to continue."

- Keep every lesson reachable in the browser, so a student who deletes the app before exams can still study.


On AllCoaching, every plan includes your own white-label Android app with your name and logo, and the iOS app is included on Pro. The website and the app run on the same academy, so you upload a lesson once.

If you already have an app that nobody installs, read what to do when no one downloads your coaching app. The short version: the problem is usually the front door, not the app.






## Too many education apps: cut the tool stack to one academy

The other side of app fatigue is tool fatigue: lessons on YouTube, notes in Drive, tests in a separate app, fees and links on WhatsApp and updates on Instagram. Moving the teaching into one academy and keeping the other tools only for reach makes life simpler for students and for you.



Five places to check, or one link. Logos belong to their owners.




#### Keep

YouTube for free lessons that bring new students. Instagram for reels and updates. WhatsApp for short reminders with one link. Each of these points to your academy.



#### Move into the academy

Paid lessons, PDF notes, tests, live class links, fee collection and student access. Anything a student has to hunt for across apps belongs in one place.


Every AllCoaching plan includes unlimited videos via YouTube, so the lessons you already record can sit inside your course without a separate video host. Meta Pixel and Google Tag Manager are included too, so you can see which posts and ads bring students who buy.


"Students do not get tired of good teachers. They get tired of hunting for the link, the PDF and the test across five apps."

Amit Ratan, Founder & CEO, AllCoaching






## How to beat app fatigue in your academy: 7 steps

Measure where students drop, put your academy on your own domain, make the first lesson free on the web, take UPI on the course page, offer the app after purchase, cut the tool stack and send one link everywhere. Most educators can do the first four in a week.


- Count where students dropFor one week, note how many people tap your link, reach the course page, install (if you use an app-first path), sign up and pay.

- Put your academy on your own domainConnect a short domain such as youracademy.in so every link students see carries your name and opens in the browser.

- Make the first lesson free on the webLet any student watch one full lesson in the browser, without installing anything or paying.

- Take UPI on the course pageShow the price, validity and language on the course page and let students pay by UPI or card there, with access opening automatically.

- Offer the app after purchaseMention your own app in the thank-you message for daily learners, and keep every lesson reachable in the browser.

- Cut the tool stackMove paid lessons, notes, tests, live class links and fees into the academy; keep YouTube, Instagram and WhatsApp for reach and reminders.

- Send one link everywherePut the same academy link in your YouTube descriptions, Instagram bio, WhatsApp messages and Telegram channel, then recount the drop-off after two weeks.




The seven steps at a glance.



### Steps 3 and 4: a free lesson and a price on one page

A free lesson in the browser lets a student judge your teaching before committing. The price, validity and language on the same page answer the questions she would otherwise send on WhatsApp. If you have not set your price yet, see how to price online courses in India, and if your first course is not ready, start with creating your first online course.






## What to tell students who won't install anything

Tell them they do not have to: send one link that opens in the browser, explain that the app is optional and say what they get in it. The message matters, because students have learned to ignore "download our app".



### Messages you can adapt


- For a new student: "The first chapter is free. Open youracademy.in/neet-biology on your phone, no app needed."

- After purchase: "Your course is live in your account on the website. If you take the daily test, the app is quicker, but everything works without it."

- To a parent: "Your child can study from any browser. No app has to be installed on your phone."



Question educators ask



### Is a marketplace app the answer to app fatigue?

It can help a little with discovery, because a student who already has one app can browse many teachers. AllCoaching courses can also be discovered on the AllCoaching app. But students still decide based on a teacher they trust, and most of your students will come from your own YouTube, Instagram and WhatsApp. Build your own academy as the base; treat any marketplace listing as a bonus.

# How to Create an Online Academy Without a Developer (2026)

Amit RatanUpdated 27 Oct 2026 · 17 min read


On this page


Start your online academy today. 7 days free.

Start free trial


You can create an online academy without a developer by using a no-code academy platform: sign up, pick a template, add your brand, build your first course from ready-made blocks, set up UPI checkout and connect your own domain. If your first module is already recorded, the build itself fits into one evening.

Picture a chemistry teacher in Lucknow with eighteen years of NEET and Class 12 batches behind him. Every time he thinks about going online, the same words stop him: app development, payment gateway, hosting, backend, developer. His teaching is ready. The technology, he assumes, is not something he can do himself.

This guide is for that teacher, and for the spoken English coach, the SSC maths educator and the yoga teacher in the same position. It is the hands-on version: what to have ready, an illustrative 6 pm to 10 pm plan, the six no-code building blocks, what you do not need, an honest developer vs no-code comparison and the fixes for common launch-night blockers. If you want the bigger picture first, read what an online academy is; for the full launch plan from course idea to first sale, see how to start an online academy in 5 steps.






## Key takeaways


- No code, no developer: a no-code academy platform gives you the website, course builder, checkout, hosting and student app as blocks you fill in.

- One evening is realistic for the build (illustrative 6 pm to 10 pm) if your first module, logo, domain name, price and PAN and bank details are ready beforehand.

- Six building blocks: template and theme, your brand, course builder, payments, your domain and your app.

- What you skip: servers, WordPress plugins to keep updated, payment code, a separate video host and app code.

- A developer still helps for custom software beyond what any platform offers, or integrations with your own systems.

- On AllCoaching: a 7-day free trial with no card, then 0% commission on Growth (₹7,999 a month) and Pro (₹14,999 a month), or Starter at ₹6,999 a year plus 10% on sales, plus GST, with your own Android app on every plan and the iOS app on Pro.







## Can you really create an online academy in one evening?

Yes, the build can fit into one evening, because a no-code platform has already built the website, checkout, hosting and app; you only fill in your content and settings. What does not fit into one evening is recording a full course, so record your first module before you start.

Ten years ago, an online academy meant a website, video hosting, a payment integration and an app, each wired together by someone technical. Today the same parts come ready-made. An academy platform works like Shopify does for shops: you sign up, choose a plan, upload your course, connect your domain and start selling, while payments, student access, apps and hosting run on their own.

So the honest answer has two halves. The software part (an academy that looks like yours, takes payments and gives students access) is an evening's work. The teaching part (lessons, notes, tests) takes as long as it takes, and that is the part only you can do.

When educators set up an academy with us, the step that runs over time is almost never the software. It is the course upload, because people try to put a whole year of lectures in on day one. Launch with one module and add the rest weekly.






## What to prepare before you start building

Have six things ready before the evening: one recorded module, its PDF notes and a test, a logo and two colours, a domain name, your PAN and bank details, and a price for the course. With these on your laptop, the evening is about clicking, not deciding.



Six things that make the evening go smoothly.


- One recorded module. Four to eight lessons of 8 to 20 minutes each, recorded on a phone with a clip-on mic. If your lessons are already on YouTube, that counts.

- PDF notes and one test. A chapter PDF and a short test for the same module. Exam students expect both.

- Logo, two colours and a photo of you. A clear photo and two lines on who you teach build more trust than an expensive logo. Do not spend weeks here.

- A domain name. Something short like youracademy.in, bought from any registrar in your own name and email, so it stays yours.

- PAN and bank details. Any payment gateway verifies your identity and bank account before it settles money to you. Our guide to accepting UPI payments for online courses lists what to keep ready.

- A price. Decide it before you sit down. Our guide on how to price online courses in India covers the methods.







## How to create an online academy without a developer: the 6 pm to 10 pm plan

Sign up, pick a template, add your brand, build your first course, set up payments, connect your domain, then test, publish and share. In that order, each block takes 15 minutes to an hour.


- Sign up and start the free trial (6:00 pm)Create your academy account on a no-code academy platform. On AllCoaching the 7-day free trial needs no card.

- Pick a template and theme (6:15 pm)Choose a website template for your home and course pages, then edit the sections, text and images.

- Add your brand (6:45 pm)Upload your logo, set two colours, and add your photo and a short paragraph on who you teach.

- Build your first course (7:15 pm)Create the course and add video lessons, PDF notes and a test in syllabus order. Mark one lesson as the free demo.

- Set up payments (8:15 pm)Set the course price and complete the payment details, so students can pay by UPI or card and get access automatically.

- Connect your domain (8:45 pm)At your domain registrar, add the records your platform shows you, copying each value exactly, so youracademy.in opens your academy.

- Test, publish and share (9:15 pm)Buy your own course once on a phone, fix anything confusing, publish, and share one link with your students.




An illustrative evening for one educator with one recorded module. Your timings will differ.

The times are illustrative. Some educators finish the brand in ten minutes and spend two hours on the course; others do the reverse. What matters is the order. Branding before the course means your course pages already look like yours as you build them. Payments before the domain means that by the time your address is live, students can buy. Testing last means you see the academy exactly as a student will.






## The no-code building blocks of an online academy

A no-code academy is six blocks: a template and theme, your brand, a course builder, payments, your domain and your app. In each one you make choices on a screen, and the platform runs the technical work underneath.



What you set up in each block, and what runs on its own.



### 1. Template and theme

Choose a website template for your academy home page and course pages, then change sections, text and images. This replaces designing and coding a website. On AllCoaching, customisable themes and templates are included on every plan, and Pro adds a premium website template.



### 2. Your brand

Upload your logo, set two colours, add your photo and a short "about" paragraph. The brand carries across the website, course pages and student app, so students see your academy's name, not a platform's.



### 3. Course builder

This is where "Build your own LMS. In just a few clicks." becomes literal. You create a course, then drag in its parts in syllabus order: video lessons, PDF notes, tests and live classes. Mark one lesson as the free demo. Every AllCoaching plan includes unlimited videos via YouTube and unlimited live classes through YouTube Live, Zoom or the built-in live room, with no hour caps.



### 4. Payments

Set the course price and complete the payment details the studio asks for. Students then pay by UPI or card at checkout, their access opens automatically, and payouts reach your bank automatically through Razorpay. You never write payment code or match screenshots on WhatsApp again.



### 5. Your domain

Point the domain you bought to your academy by adding the records your platform shows you at your registrar. It is a copy-and-paste job, and our guide to an LMS with a custom domain walks through it with the common errors.



### 6. Your app

Students who come back daily prefer an app. On AllCoaching every plan includes your own white-label Android app with your name and logo, and the iOS app is included on Pro. You do not write or maintain app code.



All six blocks live in one studio. Studio preview · sample data.

We built the studio so that the evening plan in this guide is realistic: every block above is a screen you fill in, not a project you hand to someone. Meta Pixel and Google Tag Manager are included too, so the ads and posts you run later can be measured.

## What you do not need to create an online academy

You do not need a developer, a server or hosting plan, WordPress and a stack of plugins, payment gateway code, a separate video host or app code. You still need your content, your PAN and bank details for payment verification, a domain and a few hours.



The old checklist, and what replaces each line on a no-code platform.



### No WordPress and plugins to keep alive

Many educators first try a WordPress site with an LMS plugin, a payment plugin, a video plugin and a security plugin. It can work, but each piece is software someone has to update. WordPress's own documentation advises: "Always make sure you have a current backup of your site before updating your plugins. Sometimes problems can happen during the update process." It also notes that site problems can be "caused by a conflict with different WordPress plugins".1 That is fine for a developer; it is a second job for a teacher.



The stitched-together build many educators start with, and the one-login version.



### No app to build from scratch

Building your own app from scratch means more than code. Publishing on Google Play needs a developer account with a US$25 registration fee, paid once,2 and Apple's Developer Program has an annual fee of 99 USD.3 Then come store reviews, updates for new phone versions and bug fixes, usually by the developer who built it. With a white-label academy app, the app is part of your plan instead of a separate project.



### No separate tools for each job

The other common setup is no website at all: fees on WhatsApp, notes in Drive, a new Zoom link every day and students in Excel. If that is where you are today, our guide to moving offline coaching online shows how to move it into one place.

## When you might still want a developer

Hire a developer when you need software no academy platform offers, such as a custom integration with your institute's own systems or a feature unique to your teaching method. For selling courses, tests and live classes under your own brand, you do not.


- Custom integrations. A large institute that already runs its own admissions software or ERP may want student records to flow between systems automatically.

- A one-of-a-kind learning tool. An interactive simulator, a custom practice engine or a special exam interface is real software work.

- An in-house tech team already exists. If you already pay developers, building on your own stack may make sense, as long as you budget for upkeep.

- A fully custom design. Templates and themes cover most needs. If you want a design no template allows, a designer (not necessarily a developer) can help, and the premium template on AllCoaching's Pro plan may already be enough.


What you do not need a developer for: the website, the course structure, checkout, the domain, the student app and day-to-day changes.


Question educators ask



### I already paid an agency for an app that no student uses. Should I start again?

Not from zero. Your lessons, notes, tests and student list are the valuable part, and they move with you. Set up the no-code academy during the free trial, upload your best module, connect your domain and send existing students one link. Our guide on students who only want WhatsApp covers how to bring them across.







## Common blockers on launch night, and how to fix them

Most launch-night problems are a domain that has not updated yet, payments still being verified, videos set to public, a blurry logo, too much content to upload and a test purchase that fails. Each has a quick fix, and none needs a developer.



Six blockers we see often, and what to do instead of waiting.


- Your domain does not open the academy yet. Domain changes usually take effect within minutes to a few hours and occasionally up to a day or two. Recheck that you copied each value exactly, with no extra spaces, then wait. Share the link tomorrow if you have to.

- Payments are still being verified. Gateway verification can take longer than an evening. Publish the academy with the free demo lesson visible, collect interest, and open sales once payments are active.

- A paid lesson plays for anyone on YouTube. Set lesson videos to unlisted on YouTube so they do not show in search or on your channel, and keep public videos for free lessons that bring new students in.

- The logo looks blurry. Upload a larger, square PNG with a transparent background instead of a screenshot or a WhatsApp-compressed image.

- The upload is taking all night. Stop at one complete module with its PDF and test. Publish, then add a module every week.

- The test purchase fails. Try again with UPI from a different app, check that payments are active, then message support with a screenshot of the error.



Question educators ask



### I am not good with technology at all. Will I really manage this alone?

If you can use WhatsApp and pay by UPI, you can fill in the blocks in this guide; the screens ask for things you already know, like your course name, price and photo. Take it slower than the plan: one block per evening for a week is still a launch. And during the free trial you can reach us at contact@allcoaching.in when something is unclear.







## After tonight: what to do in the first week

In the first week, buy your own course on a cheap Android phone, share one link everywhere your students already are, run a free live demo class and write down every question students ask. The academy is built; now it needs students.


- Share one link. YouTube descriptions and pinned comments, your Instagram bio, WhatsApp groups and your Telegram channel.

- Teach one live demo class. Teach one topic properly, then explain the course and share the link at the end. Our guide to running live classes from a mobile phone covers the setup.

- Fix your course page from real questions. Validity, language, doubt support and refunds are the usual ones. Answer them on the page.

- Start being found. A few helpful pages about your exam or skill bring students from Google over time. Start with our online academy SEO guide for beginners.


For the full plan from here to your first paid batch, including course structure and launch week, continue with how to start an online academy in 5 steps.






## Glossary


No-code platform
Software that lets you build and run a website, store or academy by choosing options and dragging in content, without writing code.
No-code LMS
A learning management system you set up yourself through screens and drag and drop: courses, tests, notes, live classes and student access, with no developer.
Website template
A ready-made page design for your academy's home and course pages that you edit with your own text, images and colours.
Course builder
The part of an academy platform where you create a course and add video lessons, PDF notes, tests and live classes in order.
Custom domain
Your own web address, such as youracademy.in, connected to your academy website instead of a platform's address.
White-label app
A student app that carries your academy's name and logo, built and maintained on a platform's technology.
WordPress plugin
An add-on that extends a WordPress site, such as an LMS, payment or security plugin; each one needs updating and can conflict with others.
Payment gateway
The service that collects UPI, card and net-banking payments online and settles them to your bank account for a per-transaction charge.

Is there a sales limit?No. No plan has a sales limit. Growth and Pro take 0% commission whatever you sell, and Starter takes 10% of each sale. What grows with the plan is video storage, streaming and your iOS app.

Who publishes my app on the Play Store and App Store?Your app goes on your own Google Play and Apple developer account, so it carries your name. You can publish it yourself, or give us API access to your account and we publish it for you. Google and Apple review every app, and their developer-account fees are paid to them.

How does AllCoaching work?It works the way Shopify works for an online store, built for coaching: you sign up, choose a plan, upload your course, connect your domain and start selling. Payments, course access, your apps and hosting then run automatically. There is no developer, sales call or demo involved.

Do I get my own Android and iOS app?Your own white-label Android app comes with every plan, in your name, logo and colours, alongside your website. Your own iOS app comes with Pro. The apps go on your own Play Store and App Store developer account: publish them yourself, or give us API access and we publish them for you.

Which plugins and marketing tools are included?Every plan includes plugins for Zoom, Razorpay and YouTube, with more being added, plus Meta Pixel and Google Tag Manager so you can track sign-ups and run ads to your academy. You switch them on from the studio.

Is there a free trial?Yes. Every plan comes with a 7-day free trial, so you can set up your academy, add a course and see your website before you pay, and no card is needed to start. When the trial ends, pick Growth or Pro at 0% commission, or Starter at ₹6,999 a year, to continue.

Which plan should I start with?If you are just starting and expect to sell less than about ₹7 lakh a year, Starter at ₹6,999 a year usually costs least. If you already sell, or want to keep 100% of every sale, start with Growth at ₹7,999 a month and 0% commission; choose Pro for your own iOS app, 4K video and more storage. The plan finder on this page shows the lowest-cost plan for your sales.

Is my own domain included on Starter?Yes. Every plan, including Starter, lets you connect your own domain from the studio. You buy the domain name from any registrar, usually about ₹600 to ₹1,200 a year, so it stays in your name. Until you connect one, your academy runs on a free allcoaching.in address.

What is the premium theme on Pro?Pro includes a premium theme worth ₹10,000, a more polished design for an established academy. Starter and Growth use the free themes and templates, which are fully customizable, include course pages, faculty profiles and an enquiry form, and work with your own domain.

Do I need a developer or a sales call to set up?No. You sign up, choose a plan, upload a course, connect your domain, set up payment and publish, all by yourself from the studio. There is no sales call, no demo dependency and no technical team required.

Where will students find and use my courses?Students can buy from your own website and study in your own white-label Android app (and iOS app on Pro), or on the web. Your courses can also be discovered on the AllCoaching marketplace by students searching for your exam or subject.

What happens if I upgrade, downgrade or don't renew?An upgrade takes effect as soon as payment clears, and what you already paid on Starter is credited. On Growth or Pro paid monthly you can stop any month, and the plan runs to the end of the month you paid for. To move to a lower plan, contact support and it applies from your next billing date. If you stop, your academy goes offline to students at the end of your paid period; you have 30 days to export your data or come back, and then uploaded videos are deleted.

Is marketplace discovery included on every plan?Yes. AI-driven marketplace discovery - where students search by exam, subject, language and city and find you without ad spend - is included on every plan. It is not an upgrade.

Are live classes metered separately on top of the plan price?No. Live classes are unlimited on every plan, on YouTube Live, Zoom or the built-in AllCoaching live room. There is no per-hour charge.

Can I export my data and leave anytime?Yes. Your student list, course content, payment history and analytics are exportable at any time in standard formats, in line with data-portability rights under the DPDP Act 2023. Nothing is locked - you keep ownership of your brand, your students and your content.

What happens when I reach my storage or streaming limit?Your studio shows how much you have used. When you reach a limit, extend it from the studio in a click: ₹499 a month for each extra 100 GB of storage, or ₹399 for each extra 100 GB of streaming. Until you extend or the next month starts, uploaded video pauses; your website, app, YouTube video and live classes keep running.

Are there any other charges?Prices exclude GST, which is added at checkout. Payment-gateway charges on student payments are separate and shown to you. If you need more video storage or streaming than your plan includes, you can extend it from the studio: ₹499 a month for each extra 100 GB of storage and ₹399 for each extra 100 GB of streaming. There is no setup fee and no separate charge for your domain connection or marketplace listing.

## Pricing & Plans


Is there a free trial?
Yes. Every plan comes with a 7-day free trial, so you can set up your academy, add a course and see your website before you pay, and no card is needed to start. When the trial ends, pick Starter, Growth or Pro to continue.

Full details · Pricing page




How much does AllCoaching cost for an Indian educator in 2026?
AllCoaching has three plans. Growth (₹7,999 a month) and Pro (₹14,999 a month) take 0% commission, so you keep 100% of every sale; paid yearly they cost ₹79,990 and ₹1,49,990 (2 months free). Starter is ₹6,999 a year with a 10% platform fee only on what you sell (keep 90%). There is no sales limit and no launch or setup fee on any plan. Payouts reach your bank automatically. Prices exclude GST.

Full details · Pricing page




What does the platform fee include?
Only Starter has a platform fee (10% of each sale); Growth and Pro take 0% commission. Every plan covers the UPI/card/EMI/net-banking payment checkout, HLS+AES-128 secure video streaming with DRM, anti-piracy watermarking, refund processing under Consumer Protection Rules 2020, DPDP-compliant data storage, grievance officer infrastructure, payout settlement, marketplace AI recommendation, and ongoing platform engineering. Payment-gateway charges on student payments are separate, at the gateway's rate; AllCoaching adds no markup on top.




Is there a setup fee or onboarding cost?
No setup fee. Unlike white-label app builders, which commonly charge a separate setup fee plus monthly software, AllCoaching has no launch or setup fee on any plan — Starter at ₹6,999 a year, or Growth and Pro with 0% commission from ₹7,999 a month. The branded app, academy website, marketplace listing, payment infrastructure and onboarding are included in every plan; only Starter adds a 10% platform fee when you make a sale.




Are there any hidden fees?
No hidden fees. You pay the plan price: Starter ₹6,999 a year plus 10% only on what you sell, or Growth (₹7,999 a month) and Pro (₹14,999 a month) with 0% commission. There is no launch fee, no setup fee, no per-student charge and no sales limit. Payment-gateway charges on student payments are separate, at the gateway's rate, and extra video storage or streaming is optional and prepaid from the studio.




Is AllCoaching pricing inclusive of GST?
No. Plan prices and the platform fee are exclusive of GST, which is added per Indian tax law and shown as a separate, ITC-eligible line on your invoice, so GST-registered educators can reclaim it. AllCoaching handles GST-compliant invoicing under SAC 999293.




What is AllCoaching's refund policy?
On Starter, when a student is refunded, AllCoaching reverses its 10% platform fee proportionally — a full refund reverses the full fee, a partial one reverses in proportion. Growth and Pro take 0% commission, so there is no fee to reverse. Refunds follow the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020, within 30 days. Your earned payouts on completed sales settle automatically and are not affected by an unrelated refund.

## Compliance & Tax


Is AllCoaching DPDP Act 2023 compliant?
Yes. Built DPDP-compliant from the ground up — explicit consent flows for student data, verifiable parental consent for minors under 18, data retention controls, deletion-on-request, and breach notification protocols. AllCoaching acts as data fiduciary for platform-level processing, reducing the educator's individual DPDP burden significantly.




Does AllCoaching handle GST registration and filing for educators?
AllCoaching handles GST on platform-level revenue (plan fees + platform fee). For educators, AllCoaching auto-generates GST-compliant invoices to students under SAC 999293 and provides monthly statements + GSTR-1/GSTR-3B export-ready reports. Educator must register for own GSTIN if turnover crosses ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in NE states).




What is SAC 999293 and why does it matter?
SAC 999293 is the Services Accounting Code for "commercial training and coaching services" under Indian GST law. Carries an 18% GST rate. School-level recognised education and degree institution coursework is exempt. Competitive exam coaching (NEET, JEE, UPSC, SSC, banking) typically falls under SAC 999293 and requires 18% GST collection above the turnover threshold.

Deep dive · Indian EdTech laws & regulations




Is AllCoaching IT Rules 2021 compliant?
Yes. AllCoaching has appointed a grievance officer, publishes contact details, acknowledges complaints within 24 hours, resolves within 15 days, removes infringing content on valid notice, and retains records per the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules 2021. Educators on the marketplace inherit platform-level compliance.




Does AllCoaching comply with POCSO Act for minor students?
Yes. For educators teaching students under 18, AllCoaching enforces audited communication channels, parental visibility into 1-on-1 interactions, mandatory recording of teacher-student sessions, content moderation, and POCSO-defined incident protocols. Platform provides POCSO-compliant infrastructure; individual educators remain responsible for their own conduct.




Are AllCoaching's tax invoices ITC-eligible for educators?
Yes. AllCoaching issues GST-compliant tax invoices under SAC 999293 with the platform's GSTIN, taxable value, and GST line item separated. GST-registered educators can claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) on the 18% GST charged on plan fees and the platform fee.

## Payouts & Money


When do educator payouts happen?
Automatically. Net educator earnings are settled to the registered bank account through Razorpay, our payment partner. No monthly cycle, no minimum payout threshold, no manual withdrawal request. Settlement via NEFT/RTGS/IMPS depending on amount.




What is the minimum payout amount?
No minimum threshold. AllCoaching settles whatever the educator has earned — even if it is ₹50. Automatic settlement removes the lock-in pressure of monthly payout cycles and keeps cash flow predictable.




What happens if a student requests a refund? Does it affect my payout?
Refund handling follows Consumer Protection E-Commerce Rules 2020. If approved within the published refund window, the corresponding educator earning is reversed in the next settlement. Educators can set their own refund window within legal limits (typically 7–30 days). Most educators see refund rates under 3%.




Can I change my pricing after I've enrolled students?
Yes for new enrollments; existing enrollments retain the price they paid. Educators can adjust course pricing, add bundles, run discounts, or restructure batches anytime from the studio. Platform automatically grandfather-protects existing students at their enrollment price, required under Consumer Protection rules.




07

## Security & Anti-piracy


What anti-piracy protection does AllCoaching include?
All 7 modern layers: HLS+AES-128 encryption with sub-10-second token URLs, hardware-backed DRM (Widevine L1 on Android, FairPlay on iOS, PlayReady on Windows), dynamic visible watermarking + forensic invisible watermarking per student session, device-binding with concurrent stream enforcement, geo-fencing with VPN detection, marketplace-scale Telegram/YouTube/Drive monitoring, and 24–48 hour DMCA takedown SLA.

Deep dive · 7-layer video security stack




Can students download my videos and re-sell them?
Technically very difficult. AllCoaching uses HLS+AES-128 with sub-10-second token rotation — direct download tools fail. Hardware-backed DRM prevents browser-level downloads. The only realistic vector is the "analog hole" — a student pointing a second phone camera at the screen. Forensic watermarking identifies which student session was captured, enabling targeted account suspension and legal action.




What about screen recording or screenshots?
On Android with Widevine L1, screen recording of DRM-protected video is blocked at the OS level. On iOS, FairPlay applies the same protection. Screen recording produces a black screen on protected content. Screenshots are blocked similarly. Web playback is restricted to short preview clips; full course content requires the native app.

AllCoaching Growth (₹7,999 a month) and Pro (₹14,999 a month) take 0% commission, so you keep 100% of every sale, with no sales limit; paid yearly they cost ₹79,990 and ₹1,49,990. Starter is ₹6,999 a year plus a 10% platform fee on what you sell. GST is extra on both. Yearly Starter costs ₹23,000 less upfront than Classplus's 1-year plan, and its platform fee is charged only when you make a sale.

When is Classplus cheaper than AllCoaching?
On published prices, once your sales pass about ₹2.3 lakh a year. At that point AllCoaching's yearly Starter (₹6,999 plus 10%) equals Classplus's ₹29,999 1-year price, and above it Classplus's flat price is lower on paper, unless Classplus charges a fee on your sales or payments, which its pricing page does not state. Below ₹2.3 lakh a year, AllCoaching costs less. AllCoaching Growth at 0% commission (₹7,999 a month, or ₹79,990 paid yearly) suits educators who want to keep 100% of each sale with no lock-in.

What does AllCoaching include that the Classplus price does not mention?
Every AllCoaching plan includes your own connected domain, a 7-day free trial, and a listing on the AllCoaching marketplace, where students on the AllCoaching app can find your courses. To be fair, Classplus lists unlimited storage, while AllCoaching video storage is 512 GB to 2 TB by plan, and can be extended from the studio. Both offer unlimited live classes, AllCoaching through YouTube Live, and AllCoaching adds your own iOS app on Pro (₹14,999 a month or ₹1,49,990 a year, 0% commission).

What should I ask Classplus before paying?
Ask for six things in writing: the renewal price after year one, whether GST is added, any fee on your sales or payment gateway charges, whether there is a free trial, whether your app is published under your own developer account, and how you can export your student list and content if you leave.

Can I move from Classplus to AllCoaching?
Yes, and you can do it yourself. Export your student list and content from Classplus first, start the AllCoaching 7-day free trial, build your academy, add your courses, connect your domain and set up payments. You can keep Classplus running until its term ends, so your students never lose access.

Does AllCoaching charge a setup fee or lock me in?
There is no launch or setup fee. Growth and Pro monthly have no lock-in: you can stop in any month and your plan runs to the end of the paid month. An upgrade applies as soon as you pay, with the unused value of Starter credited, and a downgrade applies from your next billing date. If you stop, your academy goes offline to students at the end of the paid period, and you have 30 days to export your content and student data or come back.

Why we built AllCoaching


# Every educator deserves an academy they can build themselves.

When teaching moved online, educators were told to get an app and a website. What they got were quotes, hidden charges and someone else holding the keys. We built AllCoaching so that any educator, technical or not, can set up a full online academy in a few clicks and start selling within a few hours.

Our story


## It started when India's classrooms went online overnight.





-
01

After COVID


### Teaching moved online, almost overnight.

When classrooms shut, educators did what they always do — they kept teaching. Zoom calls became classrooms, WhatsApp groups became study halls, YouTube became the blackboard. Students came online with them. For many teachers it was the first time their reach went beyond one town.




-
02

Then came the quotes


### Getting your own app and website came with a long bill.

Every educator was told the same thing: get your own app. What followed was a sales call, a demo and a quote — a setup fee, an app-building fee, yearly maintenance, extra for your own domain, credits for messages, and a share of sales that often showed up only after signing. The price of "your own academy" kept growing after you had already said yes.




-
03

And the dependency


### The academy had your name. The keys were with someone else.

Changing a course price meant raising a ticket. A new banner meant waiting for a developer. If the vendor stopped replying, the app stopped improving — and getting your own student list out was not always easy. Educators owned the logo on the screen, not the controls behind it.




-
04

The real gap


### Great teachers are not supposed to be tech experts.

A brilliant physics teacher should not have to learn domain settings, payment gateways and app-store rules to teach online. Most educators are not technical — and they should not need to be. The tools were built for people who already knew technology, not for the people who know teaching.




-
05

So we built AllCoaching


### An academy any educator can build alone, in a few clicks.

AllCoaching is the LMS you build yourself. Drag and drop your courses, tests, notes and live classes. Add your logo, connect your own domain, publish your own Android app (iOS app on Pro), switch on UPI payments — and start selling. No developer, no sales call, no hidden charges. A complete online academy, set up in a few hours, by you.









What we refused to copy

- Your own domain included on every plan

- You change anything yourself, any time

## The AllCoaching Manifesto: Power Back to India's Educators

**Source:** https://allcoaching.in/manifesto  
**Summary:** Education's next revolution will come from a million independent academies, not a bigger platform. Our manifesto on giving power back to India's educators.

The AllCoaching Manifesto


# Education's next revolution won't come from a bigger platform. It will come from a million independent academies.

For decades, the people who teach India have built everything except the thing they stand inside. This is our case for handing the keys back: every educator running an academy of their own, under their own name, with the technology running quietly underneath.

Build·Brand·Sell·Reach·Own
The Operating System of Education


Amit RatanFounder & CEO, AllCoaching

Updated 27 October 2026 · About 25 minutes to read


Every educator an institution. Illustration; youracademy.in is a sample domain.


Begin


00Prologue


## The quiet kranti.

Every few years, Indian education is promised a revolution. A new app, a new platform, a bigger brand on a bigger hoarding. And every few years, the people who actually teach end up holding a little less of what they built.

We think the real revolution has not happened yet. When it comes, it will not look like one giant company teaching everyone. It will look like the opposite. A physics teacher in a small town, a tutor who teaches in Hindi, an exam mentor with a loyal batch, a subject expert who has never written a line of code. Each of them running an academy of their own, under their own name, as professional as anything a large brand could put on a screen.

Not one platform with a million teachers on it. A million academies, each owned by the person who teaches in it.

India has an estimated 3.5 lakh independent educators who teach for a living: coaching-institute owners, home tutors, exam mentors, subject and skill teachers. Between them they hold more knowledge than any company ever will. Most of them teach on borrowed ground. Someone else's building, someone else's app, someone else's platform. They have the knowledge. What they have rarely had is the infrastructure, and the control over it.

Teaching has always been powerful in India. Owning the teaching has rarely been in the teacher's hands.
This manifesto is about changing that. It is long, because the problem is old and the change we are arguing for is large. It sets out how education came to be owned by everyone except the teacher, why the obvious fixes failed, what we believe should replace them, and what we are building at AllCoaching to make it ordinary.

We call it the Operating System of Education. You build the academy. We run everything beneath it.

We are not neutral about any of this. We are on the educator's side. If that makes this a manifesto rather than a brochure, good. A brochure describes a product. A manifesto describes the world you want, and then holds you to it.




01How education was owned


## Every era moved the keys further from the teacher.

Before saying what we believe, we have to be honest about how we got here. Look at the last few decades of Indian teaching as three eras, and a pattern appears.






Who holds the keys, era by era. Our reading of history, drawn as an illustration.






### The building era: the walls owned the business

For a generation, a teaching career began with a room. A hall above a sweet shop, a rented floor near the railway station, a board painted by hand and a bench that seated more students than it was built for. The teacher could be brilliant, but the reach of that brilliance was set by geography: how far a student could cycle, which city had an exam culture, which family could afford a hostel in a coaching town.

Those who grew did it by renting more space, in more expensive places, under bigger hoardings. Rent rose before income did. The best location, not the best lesson, decided who was found first. A great teacher in the wrong lane stayed small. In the building era, the landlord and the location owned the business, and the teacher paid for both.



### The app era: someone else held the keys

Then the classroom closed, and everything moved into a phone. Almost overnight an educator needed a website, an app, a payment page and a way to stream classes. Most did not have a developer, so they hired someone who did. Agencies arrived with quotes, demos and setup fees. They built the app, held the code, managed the store listing and billed for every change.

The educator's name was on the icon. The keys were in someone else's pocket. Want a new course page? Raise a ticket. Want to change a price? Wait for the developer. Want to leave? Start again from nothing. In the app era, the vendor owned the controls, and the teacher paid for those too.



### The platform era: the teacher became supply

The third era looked like a rescue. Large EdTech platforms offered reach, polish and a ready audience. Many good teachers joined them, and some did well for a while. But slowly, the teacher's own name became smaller than the platform's. Students enrolled with the brand, not the person. Recordings, reviews and student lists stayed with the platform. Prices, promotion and visibility were decided somewhere else.

In the platform era, the platform owned the student relationship. The teacher became inventory, a face on a thumbnail inside someone else's catalogue.

Three eras, three owners: the landlord, the agency, the platform. Each brought something real. Each moved a little more power away from the person doing the teaching.

The room gave students a place to gather. The app took teaching beyond the city. The platform brought scale. We are not dismissing any of it. We are pointing at what each era cost: a little more of the educator's control, a little more of their margin, a little more of their name.

We think the fourth era turns that around. Not by going back to the room, and not by building a bigger platform, but by giving every educator the infrastructure that only large institutions used to have, and leaving the ownership with them.


What we mean by revolution
Not louder marketing. Not a bigger platform. A kranti in who owns the means of teaching: the brand, the students, the price, the data and the decisions.

When those sit with the educator, everything else in Indian education starts to rearrange itself around good teaching instead of around rent, vendors and ad budgets.





02The right dream, sold the wrong way


## "Own your academy" was never the mistake.

When classrooms went dark in 2020, Indian educators were handed an idea: build your own academy online. Your name. Your students. Your income.

Video calls became classrooms, WhatsApp groups became study halls, and a wave of app-building companies promised every teacher a branded app of their own. Teachers who had never thought of themselves as business owners suddenly were.

The dream was right. An educator should own their brand, their students and their income. What went wrong was how it was sold.

Owning an academy usually meant calling a sales team, sitting through a demo, negotiating a quote, paying a setup fee, and then waiting weeks while somebody else built the thing. Every change needed a support ticket. Every new feature came with a price. The educator owned the logo on the screen, but not the controls behind it.

And once the app went live, most educators were left alone with it. No students arrived on their own. The app was a mohalle ki coaching centre that had gone digital, but stayed just as invisible, just as local, just as limited. It had moved online without gaining any of the internet's reach.

The problem was never that educators wanted their own academy. The problem was that someone else held the keys, and nobody helped students find the door.
Many educators drew the wrong lesson from those years. Some decided that owning an academy was a vanity project, that the only realistic path was to join a large platform and accept its terms. Others kept paying for an app they could not change, because starting over felt worse.

The real lesson is different. It is not "stop building your own academy." It is this: an educator should be able to build it themselves, in minutes, without a developer, and it should not leave them alone once it is live. Ownership without control is a costume. Control without reach is a locked room. The educator needs both, and needs them without asking anyone's permission.

That is the idea this manifesto is built on.




03The educator's trap


## Developer, marketer, payments desk. Teacher last.

Here is what nobody told the educators who went online: having an academy and running an academy are two completely different jobs.

The companies that built their apps were paid when the app was delivered. Everything after that was the educator's problem. So educators did what entrepreneurs do. They tried everything.

They became entertainers. Social feeds reward what is dramatic or amusing, so educators began chasing views instead of teaching depth. A chemistry teacher who spent years mastering reaction mechanisms now spent evenings scripting sixty-second reels. The quality of instruction fell in proportion to the pressure to perform for an algorithm.

They spent on marketing instead of education. With nothing bringing students to them, acquisition became a paid game. A small educator with a modest monthly ad budget was bidding for the same attention as companies spending crores. That was never a fair fight, and it was never a contest of who teaches better.

Every rupee spent on ads is a rupee not spent on a better curriculum. Every hour making reels is an hour not spent preparing a better class.
They became technically dependent. Checkout pages that failed at the worst moment, video hosting that cost more as they grew, app updates that needed a developer, login problems that landed on the educator's own phone at eleven at night. Every teacher became an accidental startup founder, without the funding, the team or the tools.

They met hidden costs at every turn. Setup fees. Paid add-ons. Transaction cuts. Annual maintenance. Charges that only appeared after signing. What started as "your own platform" carried a cost structure most educators never saw clearly until it was too late to walk away.





Pain 01

#### Someone else holds the keys

The academy carries your name, but every change goes through a sales rep, a developer or a support ticket. Ownership in name, dependency in practice.

Pain 02

#### Performing replaces teaching

Algorithm-driven reach rewards entertainment, not instruction. The best educators are not always the most viral, and the feed rewards virality, not pedagogy.

Pain 03

#### Marketing eats quality

Every rupee spent on paid acquisition is taken from curriculum, better tools or a co-teacher. Educators are forced to choose between growing and teaching well.

Pain 04

#### The tech burden

Payments, video, app updates, logins. Educators end up running a technology company they never signed up for, with no technology team behind them.

Pain 05

#### Hidden costs, opaque cuts

Setup fees, paid add-ons, gateway cuts and renewal surprises quietly eat into the margin of every sale.

Pain 06

#### Alone after launch

A standalone academy is visible only to people who already know you exist. No shared discovery, no network, no new students arriving on their own.





The cost of the trap is not only money. It is attention. Teaching well needs long, unbroken hours: reading, preparing, solving, rehearsing an explanation until it lands. The trap breaks those hours into pieces and hands them to vendors, feeds and spreadsheets.

Over time it changes who succeeds. Not the most patient teacher, not the clearest explainer, but the one who can best tolerate being a part-time developer and a full-time marketer. That is a selection system that filters out exactly the people students need most. Any revolution in Indian education has to start by switching it off.




04The student's side


## Great teachers, hidden behind walls.

We spend most of this manifesto talking about educators. But the student's side of the story is just as broken, and in the end it is the reason any of this matters.

Consider a student in Patna preparing for SSC CGL. A friend has mentioned a good reasoning teacher. The student goes looking. They find a reel, then a Telegram channel, then an app link that asks them to download, register, verify an OTP and trust a payment page they have never seen before. Then they do it again for the maths teacher. And again for English. Each step is a place where a nervous student, spending a family's money, can decide not to trust what they see.

The best teacher in India is invisible if students cannot find them, and unconvincing if what they find does not look like a real academy.
Two things decide whether that student enrols. First: can they find the teacher at all? Second: when they arrive, does it feel like a real academy they can trust? A proper website, a clear course page, a familiar way to pay, an app with the teacher's name on it.

Most independent educators fail on one or both. Not because their teaching is weak, but because what surrounds the teaching is broken. A course that a student never finds, or finds and does not trust, is not a content failure. It is an infrastructure failure.


A question that exposes everything
How does a student in Jaipur, looking for the best biology teacher for NEET, find a teacher with a small YouTube channel and no ad budget? Today, mostly, they don't. They end up with whoever advertised most, not whoever taught best. And if they do find the right teacher, they often land on a WhatsApp number and a UPI ID instead of an academy.


There is a quieter cost too. When discovery is bought, students learn to judge teachers by production value and follower counts. Prices drift up to pay for the ads. The family in a small town ends up paying for a marketing budget, not for better teaching.

Fixing this means giving every educator two things at once: a professional academy under their own name, and a way to be found by students who don't know them yet. One without the other fails the student as surely as it fails the teacher.




05Big EdTech is not the educator's friend


## Not partnership. Absorption.

The case for joining a giant EdTech platform sounds reasonable: reach, infrastructure, brand trust, students handed to you. Why not just join?

Let us be precise about what we are arguing. This is not about any one company, and it is not about the people inside them, many of whom care deeply about students. It is about a model. A model in which the platform is the brand and the educator is supply. Once you see the model, its outcomes stop being surprising.

Your brand disappears. Students enrol with the platform, not with you. If you leave, the students, the reviews and the history stay behind. You leave with nothing you can carry.

Your content becomes their asset. The lectures, notes and question banks you created keep selling the next batch, with or without you.

Your income is never fully yours. Revenue splits are rarely transparent, and the platform takes the larger share because it controls discovery.

Your growth is capped by their algorithm. The platform promotes whatever grows platform revenue. Some days that is you. Many days it is not. You are competing with your own platform's interests.

A platform that owns the student relationship will always, in the end, optimise for itself. That is not malice. It is gravity.





What an educator needsTypical agency-built appTypical big platformAllCoaching

Your own brand: domain, logo, appYesNoYes

Start without a sales call or demoNoPartlyYes
Discovery beyond your own followersNoPartlyYes

Fees published before you startPartlyNoYes
Export your courses, students and dataPartlyNoYes






An agency-built app gives you a brand, but no control and no reach. A big platform gives you reach, but takes your brand. Indian educators have been stuck between these two models for years, told that this is simply how the market works. There is a third way, and it starts by noticing that the choice itself was manufactured.




06The false choice


## Ownership or reach. Never both, they said.

For half a decade, every option in Indian EdTech asked educators to give something up. Own your academy, and accept that you are on your own. Join a platform, and accept that you are a listing on someone else's shelf.

We think that choice was never real. It came from how the tools were built and how they made money, not from anything educators or students needed.

Ownership and reach are not opposites. They only looked that way because nobody built one thing that gave an educator both.
Look at how good shopkeepers work. A shop owner has their own signboard, their own counter, their own regular customers who come straight to them. They also sit in a market where new customers walk past every day. Nobody asks them to choose between their shop and the market. The shop is theirs. The market brings footfall. And the more good shops a market has, the more people come to it, which helps every shop in it.

Educators deserve the same arrangement. Their own academy, on their own domain, under their own name, built and run by them. And alongside it, a shared marketplace where students who are looking for a teacher can find them, so that every educator who joins makes it a little easier for every other educator to be discovered.



The academy is the star; discovery is the sky around it. Illustration with sample labels.

Notice the order. The academy comes first. Discovery supports it. A marketplace that replaces the academy is just another platform. A marketplace that sends students to academies is a public good for teachers.

That is the layer Indian education has been missing. Not another app. Not another platform. A foundation that lets each educator build their own academy, and quietly connects all of them.




07The Operating System of Education


## You build the academy. We run everything beneath it.

We describe AllCoaching as the Operating System of Education deliberately. Not an app-building agency. Not a platform that rents you a shelf. An operating system.



You build on top. Everything beneath runs on its own.

An operating system does not decide what you build on it. It does the invisible work underneath, so that you can build exactly what you want on top. Nobody thinks about the operating system on their phone while they are calling their mother. That is the point. It is there so that the important thing can happen without friction.

For an educator, the important thing is teaching. So AllCoaching is built as layers that run underneath every academy, the same way for a single tutor and for a multi-teacher institute.

Our economics are tied to the educator's success. When educators sell more, we earn more. That is not a slogan. It is the business model.



08The economic shift


## What changes when educators own the means of teaching.

Revolutions are usually described in speeches. This one is easier to see in a ledger.

In every earlier era, the educator's economics were set by someone else: the rent the landlord asked, the quote the agency sent, the split the platform decided. Costs were discovered after signing. Margins were whatever was left. When the educator owns the academy and the terms are written down in advance, four things change at once.

Data is exportable. This is the quiet clause that makes all the others honest. If an educator can leave with their courses, students and data, then we have to keep earning their stay. A platform you cannot leave does not need to be good. One you can leave does.

When the educator owns the academy, every rupee saved on rent, vendors and opaque cuts can go back into the one thing students pay for: better teaching.
This is the economic heart of the revolution. Not lower prices for their own sake. We are not, and will never position ourselves as, the low-cost option. What changes is who keeps the value. Under borrowed ground, value leaks to whoever holds the keys. On owned ground, it compounds for the person doing the work, and through them, for the students they teach.




09The next decade


## Every educator an institution.

A manifesto should be clear about the line between what exists and what it hopes for. So here it is, drawn plainly.

What follows under Today is true now. What follows under Next and The decade ahead is belief and direction: the world we think Indian education is moving towards, and the world we intend to help build. None of it is a product announcement.





TodayTrue now


### An educator can own an academy in an afternoon.

The tools that once needed an agency and a quote are now self-serve. That alone is a break from every era before it.


- Sign up, choose a plan, upload a course, connect a domain and start selling, with no sales call, demo or developer.

- The academy carries the educator's name: a website on their own domain, their own Android app on every plan, and the iOS app on Pro.

- The educator keeps 100% of every sale on Growth and Pro (90% on Starter), on a price published before sign-up.

- 500+ educators are already selling on AllCoaching.





NextBelief & direction


### The small-town academy stops looking small.

We believe the gap between a single teacher and a large institution will close, not because the institutions shrink, but because the teacher's infrastructure grows up.


- Every educator an institution. One teacher with the systems that only big institutes used to afford: admissions, payments, classes, records, an app, a website, all running together.

- A teacher in a small town runs an academy as professional as the biggest brands. The student cannot tell from the screen whether the academy has one teacher or a hundred. They can only tell whether the teaching is good.

- Technology disappears into the background. Setting up, getting paid and giving access become as unremarkable as electricity. The teacher only teaches.

- Students choose teachers by quality, not ad budget. As more good academies are discoverable side by side, reputation earned in the classroom starts to outweigh reach bought in a feed.





The decade aheadBelief & direction


### A network of academies, not a handful of giants.

Ten years from now, we believe Indian education will look less like a few towers and more like a city: millions of independent academies, each with its own door, connected by shared streets.


- Education as a network of independent academies. Not a few giant platforms deciding who is seen, but a mesh of educator-owned academies where students move freely to whoever teaches them best.

- Regional and Hindi-medium educators become national names. The finest teacher of a subject in Hindi, Bengali, Tamil or Marathi should be reachable by every student who learns in that language, wherever they live.

- AI as the educator's assistant, never their replacement. We believe new tools should take the drudgery off a teacher's desk so they have more time to teach, and that the relationship between a student and a teacher should stay human. This is a belief about how such tools should be used, not a feature we are announcing.

- An educator's brand and students belong to the educator, for life. A reputation built over decades should never be stranded inside someone else's product. It should move with the teacher, the way a degree or a good name does.





None of this happens because one company wills it. It happens because enough educators decide, one academy at a time, that they will no longer teach on borrowed ground. Our job is to make that decision easy, and to keep the infrastructure honest while they make it.




10The manifesto


## Our promise to every educator who ever deserved more.

Seven beliefs we were founded on, and three we are adding as we look at the decade ahead. Hold us to all ten.


01

### We believe teaching is a vocation, not a startup.

An educator should never have to become a developer, a marketer or a payments desk to run an academy. The technology should disappear so the teaching can come first.

02

### We believe every educator should own their academy.

Their name on the website, their logo on the app, their students in their list, their data exportable at any time. An educator's brand is not a listing on someone else's shelf.

03

### We believe an educator should be able to build it themselves.

No sales call, no demo, no agency, no waiting. If an educator can teach a class, they can build their academy in a few clicks, and change it whenever they want.

04

### We believe ownership and reach should not be a trade-off.

An educator should have their own academy and still be found by students who don't know them yet. Every educator who joins AllCoaching makes the marketplace stronger for every other educator.

05

### We believe a student should find the best teacher, not just the most advertised one.

The best biology teacher in Kanpur should be reachable by a student in Kochi. Distance and ad budgets should stop deciding who gets found. Merit should.

06

### We believe prices should be published before anyone signs up.

What we charge and what the educator keeps is written down in the open. One published plan price, 0% commission on Growth and Pro, and no surprises after the fact.

07

### We are honest about what we are building and what it will take.

AllCoaching is not a magic solution. Having your own academy doesn't guarantee overnight success. What it guarantees is a fair foundation, one where your success depends on the quality of your teaching, not on your budget or technical skills. We give you the tools. The rest is yours to win.

08

### We believe technology should be invisible.

The best infrastructure is the kind nobody notices. If an educator is thinking about servers, app stores or payment gateways, we have not done our job yet.

09

### We believe an educator's students belong to the educator.

The relationship between a teacher and the students they taught is not inventory. It is not ours to keep, sell or redirect. It goes wherever the educator goes.

10

### We believe reach should be earned by teaching, not bought.

Advertising will always exist, and educators are free to use it. But a teacher who teaches well should be able to grow without outbidding anyone. Good teaching should be the strongest signal there is.

## Amit Ratan, Founder & CEO of AllCoaching: The Story

**Source:** https://allcoaching.in/author/amit-ratan  
**Summary:** Amit Ratan, founder and CEO of AllCoaching: from a coaching directory in Prayagraj in 2018 to the academy platform educators build themselves, without a developer.

Founder · AllCoaching


The founder's story



# Amit Ratan. Ten years building for India's teachers.

I watched a brilliant teacher go unheard because he had no way to reach students. Ten years, one collapsed website and five years of rebuilding later, AllCoaching lets every educator run their own academy, without a developer and without asking anyone's permission.
